I, Theodinus, bishop of the see of Porto and Santa Rufina, have subscribed. I, Henry, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. [Col. 1367C] I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri, have subscribed. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Roland, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Radulf, cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Transmundus, notary of the Holy Roman Church, in the fourth indiction, in the year 1185 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Pope Urban III.

XXIII. He confirms the agreement made between the bishop of Saintes and the monks of Ais concerning the church of La Rochelle and certain other matters in the diocese of Saintes. (Verona, March 4.)

[Same work, p. 1449.]

[Col. 1367D]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HUGH, abbot, and the convent of Cluny: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily grant assent to the just desires of petitioners, and bring to fulfilment, with the resulting effect, vows which do not depart from the path of reason. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, willingly concurring in your just petitions, we confirm by apostolic authority for you and your church, and strengthen by the protection of this present writing, the agreement made between your monks of Ais and Peter, archpriest of La Rochelle, by Bernard, once bishop of Saintes, of good memory, and accepted by both parties, just as it is contained in his authentic instrument. For greater permanence in the future, we have caused it to be entered in these present letters. Its text is as follows:

In the name of the holy and undivided Trinity. I, Bernard, by God’s grace bishop of Saintes, wish it to be known to my successors and to all who read this charter how the dispute which had arisen between Peter, archpriest of La Rochelle, and the monks of Ais was settled peacefully. For I had often heard the monks’ complaint against Peter, [Col. 1368A] the archpriest, whom Reginald, prior of Ais, had presented to us to be chaplain. He unjustly withheld from them the rights in offerings which, as they maintained, appeared to belong to them. Unable any longer to endure this, both because of the admonition of Lord Geoffrey, archbishop of Bordeaux, a friend nevertheless of the Church of Cluny, and because of the command of Pope Eugenius, who had laid this upon me orally at the Council of Reims, I satisfied the monks’ complaint and wish.

The monks said that, in the time of William Gardrad, bishop of Saintes, Arnold, prior of Ais, and Reginald Durannus, chaplain, used to divide equally the offerings made in the aforesaid church. This was testified to us by trustworthy men: namely Giraud of Allodium, chaplain; [Col. 1368B] Geoffrey Veritas, chaplain of Château d’Allion; Maurinus of Comnia; Stephen Bernardi; and Stephen of Fonte, parishioners of that church; and Audoin and Aimeric, servants of Ais, who used to receive the offerings from the hand of the chaplain himself at the altar.

Encouraged by their testimony, with the assent of both parties we ordained and confirmed that offerings made in any manner in the church of St. Mary of Comnia should be divided equally between the chaplain and the monks. The sole exception is the coin which the chaplain receives for the chaplaincy, if it is offered at the Mass which he has sung. If an offering is made to the chaplain during a visitation of the sick, such as a single coin, it shall be his alone. But if a sick person wishes to confer from his money [Col. 1368C] or from any noble rent either upon the church of Ais or upon the chaplain some benefaction, it shall be divided equally. Lands, vineyards, houses, and other buildings shall belong to the monks.

The confessions of parishioners and of other visitors, whether in Lent, Advent, or another season, shall be divided equally. With respect to wax and candles offered in the church, the church shall be served jointly by the chaplain and the monks. Whatever remains from the Paschal candle and other candles shall be divided equally. If the monks wish to have half of the offering made on the Monday after the parish Mass, they shall not be forbidden. They, together with the chaplain, shall jointly provide for the bishop’s procuration.

If any monk wishes to receive the offering presented into the priest’s hand, or if the prior directs someone to receive it, he shall receive it; afterwards it shall be placed openly upon the altar, until, after Mass, in the absence of the clerics, it is divided equally. [Col. 1368D] On feast days, if the prior of Ais or the prior of La Rochelle is present, he shall be invited by the chaplain to sing the solemn Mass. If either wishes to sing, he shall not be forbidden. On feast days on which it is customary to give something to the clerics, we forbid the chaplain alone to give them anything without the will and assent of the monks.

If the monks wish to ring Matins and the other hours of the day, as is their custom, they shall ring and sing without hindrance from the clerics. The clerics also shall sing without hindrance from the monks. The chaplain shall introduce his subchaplains into the church with the counsel of the prior of Ais. If they commit anything for which they ought to be removed, they shall be removed with the prior’s counsel, and others shall be installed in their place.

Moreover, lest this decree of ours, thus established, should be overturned by any cavilling of chaplains or monks who may come after, the authority of our privileged letters has been applied. These things were done at Gratiam-Dei, on the tenth day before the Kalends of October, in the year 1149 of the Lord’s Incarnation, when Eugenius III was Roman pontiff, Louis was reigning king in France, and the same man was duke in Aquitaine. Witnesses are the aforementioned men: Arnold, abbot of Gratiam-Dei; Geoffrey, archdeacon; William Aleard, almoner; Jordan of Saintes, [Col. 1369A] prior of Anesio; Aimeric, prior of Boeth; and, from the monks of Ais, Stephen Constantinus and John of Moguir, with many others.

Furthermore, we likewise confirm for you by apostolic authority, and strengthen by the protection of this present writing, the grant canonically made to you by our venerable brother Adhemar, bishop of Saintes, just as it is contained in his authentic instrument. The text of that instrument is as follows:

I, Adhemar, by God’s grace bishop of Saintes, inclined by the prayers of the venerable Lord Theobald, abbot of Cluny, and attentive to the peace and tranquillity of the brethren of Cluny, grant and confirm by episcopal authority, to be possessed and held forever by you and your successors, the monasteries, churches, and chapels situated in our diocese, as well as all tithes of your churches and of other churches, should you be able to recover them from laymen, whether by gifts, [Col. 1369B] settlements, exchanges, purchases, or other lawful means, wherever they may be, and likewise everything whatsoever which, God being favourable, you may be able to acquire.

Moreover, we grant and confirm to you and your successors in perpetuity every gift or grant which Lord Hisembert of Château d’Allion is known to have made to the church of Ais with the counsel of prudent men, as the tenor of his authentic instrument declares. And, so that the grant and confirmation may obtain the strength of perpetual validity, we have caused this page to be secured by the protection of our seal. For still greater security, so that every ground of dispute may be removed, we give and grant you the tithes which you have acquired, or may acquire, from laymen.

We also prohibit, under pain of excommunication, all laymen who hold tithes in your parishes from presuming, under any title, to transfer them to other churches. If they presume to do so, let them be deprived of burial and of every divine office. As written above, we have done this with the counsel of Henry, archdeacon of Aluiciensis. Moreover, lest this decree of ours, thus established, be overturned by any cavilling of those who may come after, we have caused it to be secured by the impression of our seal.

This charter was made at Saintes, on the thirteenth day before the Kalends of July, in the year 1182 of the Lord’s Incarnation, when Lucius III was Roman pontiff, Philip was reigning king in France, and Henry, king of the English, governed the duchy of Aquitaine through his son Richard. Witnesses are the aforesaid archdeacon; Master William Testaudus, our notary; William Viviani; Arnold, monk and our nephew; Giraud, archpriest of Archiac; Bernard, abbot of Nantolium; Master Henry, companion of the lord abbot of Cluny; Siguin; Robert, notary of the same abbot; Elias of Fors; Master Columbus; Durannus Cambarlangus; Hugh, marshal; and Robert, priest, who wrote the charter.

Therefore let no person at all be permitted to infringe this page [Col. 1370A] of our confirmation or rashly act against it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, on the fourth day before the Nones of March.

XXIV. He receives under protection the nunnery of St. Peter of Luco and confirms its goods and privileges. (Verona, March 13.)

[MITTARELLI, *Annals of Camaldoli*, IV, appendix, p. 135.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughter the abbess of St. Peter of Luco and her sisters, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

For prudent virgins, who under the habit of religion, with lamps kindled by works of holiness, prepare themselves to go forth to meet the Bridegroom, apostolic protection ought to be present, lest perhaps an assault of any rashness call them back from their purpose or—God forbid—break the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved daughters in Christ, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and, following the example of Pope Eugenius, our predecessor of happy memory, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery of St. Peter, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing.

We decree that whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, with the Lord’s help, by concession of pontiffs, grant of kings or princes, offering of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and those who succeed you. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: whatever is in the town of Luco; whatever you possess in the estate of Larciana; properties in Filiano, Fortunio, and Prata; part of Cantamerulo; part of Riofrigido with its appurtenances; [Col. 1370B] part of Rivocornoclario with its appurtenances; and part of the estate of Castrum and of the estates of Silva and Frena with their appurtenances.

Furthermore: the churches of St. Mary of Riofrigido, St. Bartholomew, St. Nicholas, St. George of Luco, and St. Christina near the castle of Seven Fountains, with their appurtenances. Since you have freely and without opposition held their administration for forty years and more, just as you justly and peacefully possess them, we confirm them to you and to your church by apostolic authority.

No one shall presume to demand or extort tithes from you on lands newly brought under cultivation which you cultivate by your own hands or resources, or on the produce of your animals. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordinations of clerics to be promoted to holy orders from the diocesan bishop, if he is Catholic, has the favour and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to provide these to you freely and without any abuse; otherwise you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, may grant what is requested.

Furthermore, we decree that the burial place of that house shall be free, so that the devotion and last will of those who determine to be buried there may be fulfilled, unless perhaps, etc. (The remainder as in the bull of Eugenius III, year 1146, 7 Ides of February.)

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Conrad, archbishop of Mainz, have subscribed. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of St. Mark, [lacuna] have subscribed. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of St. Mary across the Tiber, have subscribed. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the title of the Twelve Apostles, have subscribed. [Col. 1371C] I, Albinus, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Melior, cardinal priest of the title of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Adelard, cardinal priest of the title of St. Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Soffredus, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Roland, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. [Col. 1371D] I, Rodulf, cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

Done at Verona, through the hand of Transmundus, notary of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Ides of March, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1185 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban III.

XXV. He receives under protection the monastery of St. Apollinaris at Classe and confirms its goods and privileges. (Verona, March 15.)

[Same work, p. 137.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BERNARD, abbot of St. Apollinaris in Classe, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

[Col. 1372A] Those choosing the religious life ought to have protection at hand, lest perhaps an assault of any rashness call them back from their purpose or—God forbid—break the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and, adhering to the footsteps of Pope Alexander, our predecessor of happy memory, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves your church, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing.

First, we decree that the monastic order known to have been established in your church according to God, the Rule of blessed Benedict, and the institution of the Camaldolese brethren shall be observed there inviolate for all time. Furthermore, whatever possessions or goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the Lord’s provision, through concessions of pontiffs, grants of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

In the county of Perugia, five cells: namely St. Severus; the chapel of St. Margaret in the estate of Saliatica; the monastery of St. Peter on the Hill; St. Peter in the valley of Ponte beside the Tiber; and the monastery of St. Fortunatus, situated on the opposite bank of the Tiber.

In the county of Gubbio, the estate called Bignoli; the court called Praetorium; another called Baroncelli; and a third called Nartianula, with everything belonging to them.

In the county of Fermo, the entire court called Campolungo; the castle called Pausuli; another called Praetorium; half the castle of Casale, and half of the castle, with half of its churches; the court of St. Mary in Cerbaria and St. Apollinaris of Potentia; the monastery of St. Peter of Butrio with the estate of the tower and the marsh called Rota. The boundaries of that Rota are: on the first side, the river Tenc; on the second, the seashore; on the third, the land of St. Blaise; and on the fourth, the land of St. Mary. Also, whatever you possess in the court of St. Elpidius and St. Julian, and at Monte Lupone and Murrivalli, with the tithes and first fruits of the land of your demesne and of your men, granted by Azo, bishop of Fermo, of blessed memory; its boundaries are: on the first side, the Potentia; on the second, the Tenna; on the third, the seashore; and on the fourth, Camerino.

In the county of Senigallia, the estate of Menolaria; the holding of Maurus; and the three estates of Ingallati, Arilla, and Donatianum. Within the city, the church of St. Mary of the Scots.

In the county of Fano, the entire place called Raviniana, with churches and everything belonging to it; on the first side, the Suasanus River and the land of St. Lawrence; on the second, Sassobrata and the river called Maturius; on the third, the land of Fossombrone; and on the fourth, the water called Albella. In the same county, the castle of Albiniano and the fortress of Sambatica; in the city, the church of St. Apollinaris beside the wall, the church of St. Vitus, and the church of St. Christopher.

In the city of Pesaro, the monastery of St. Decentius with all that it possesses within and outside the city; the estate called Fresuli; the place called Vallicella; the castle of Florentius; and the estate of Ravignano.

In the county of Rimini, the castle of Gaius with its court; the estate of Uzani; whatever you possess in the castle of Lunziano; in the court, the place called Fontana Sabbatina and Faturia; the court of Sale, with its boundaries: on the first side, the seashore; on the second, Pisatellus; on the third, Vetretum and Paverianus; and on the fourth, the boundary called Arzer, running from the meadow as far as *la Stratella*, and the Fabrica stream running down into the sea; and what you possess at Castagneto: Branchise, Bulgaria, and Bulgarnovo; the court of Casalicli; and the castle of Pisatellus with its court.

In the county of Montefeltro, the estate of Rusciano. In the Saxenate, the court of St. Angelus of the Plain and the castle of Livorius. In the county of Cesena, the estate of Cazani with the church of St. Michael; what came from Rainulf of the castle of Gallisidium, with his wife, within that same castle; and his court, situated in the counties of Rimini and Cesena; half the court of Verignano, situated in the county of Rimini; whatever you also possess in the city and territory of Saxenate; and the court of Succuniano with the church of St. Apollinaris.

In the county of Forlimpopoli, the court called Bagnolum with its castle and church. In the county of Forlì, the estate of Barisani and the court of Pertusiacum with the church established there. In the county of Faenza, the court called Quadrata, with estates and holdings: namely the estates of Frentula, Susiana, Pituli, Greater and Lesser Saltus, Granariolum, Lake Ceredum, and Praesentianum; and the castle of Pergula.

In the district of Imola, the monastery called St. Peter, the estate called Quinta, and the estate called Solustra. In the territory of Ravenna, the church of St. Martin with the entire court called Aqualonga; St. Mary in Beatiano; and St. Mary in Pratella, with all their appurtenances: on the first side, the Ursaria bank and the church of St. Gervasius, with the properties adjacent to it as far as the seashore; on the second, the seashore for three miles below the sea itself, as far as the port of Classe; on the third, Classatellus and the boundary between you and St. Severus, reaching the two *masinae* at Stratella, which goes to the well of Tressi, and the old course of the Rapheda water as far as the forks; on the fourth side, the estate called Bagnolum and Saxanum, and thus it proceeds through Stadilianum as far as Sapim.

Within the city of Ravenna, the church of St. Mary in Peace and St. Mary in Hortale, with houses and gardens; St. Barbara; and St. Mary in Bologna, with their appurtenances. In the county and city of Ficocle, whatever you possess: namely saltworks and *tumbae* (mounds), houses and lands, vineyards and woods. In the county of Fossombrone, the church of St. Sophia with all its appurtenances. In the county of Bologna, the right which you possess in the church of St. Mary in Cavalli, with its lands, woods, marshes, and fisheries; and whatever came to you from Lady Arachele, namely the estate of Tumba with all its appurtenances; from the men of Peter Azo; from Benno of Liucia; and from Liuzo, son of Hugh Lucius; the estate in the place called Palatiolo, which the daughter of Manfred Wiciard left; and also the tithes which you canonically possess. We confirm these to you and to your church by apostolic authority.

No one shall presume to demand tithes from you on your newly cultivated lands which you cultivate by your own hands or resources, or on the produce of your animals.

It shall also be lawful for you to receive clerics and laymen, free and absolved, who flee from the world to conversion, and to retain them without any opposition. We further forbid any of your brethren, after making profession in the same place, to leave your cloister through any levity; and no one shall dare to retain one who has left without a letter of authorization from the community. We decree that the burial place of that house shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who have resolved to be buried there—unless they are excommunicated or under interdict—saving the right of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken.

We hold ratified and firm the liberties and dignities granted to your church and its ancient and reasonable customs, and decree that they shall remain unimpaired for all time. Furthermore, just as I [name lost in the source], cardinal priest of the basilica of the Twelve Apostles and legate of the Apostolic See—to whom Pope Alexander, our predecessor of happy memory, committed for hearing the dispute that had arisen between you and the monks of the new St. Apollinaris concerning the body of that martyr—is known to have established by prudent deliberation that no one should presume to venerate the body of the same martyr, which he found at your monastery, in any other place as though it were present there, except in your monastery at Classe: so we also hold the constitution of that cardinal ratified and firm, and confirm it by apostolic authority.

Moreover, we have thought fit to confirm for you by apostolic authority the liberty granted to your monastery by Walter, sometime archbishop of Ravenna, of good memory, as it is contained in his authentic instrument and as your predecessors and you yourselves have hitherto enjoyed it.

Therefore we decree that no one, etc. But if anyone, etc. Seal.

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Henry, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of St. Mark, have subscribed. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of St. Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the title of the Twelve Apostles, have subscribed. [Col. 1375A] I, Albinus, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Melior, cardinal priest of the title of Pammachius of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Adelard, cardinal priest of the title of St. Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Soffredus, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Roland, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Rodulf, cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

[Col. 1375B] Given at Verona, through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the Ides of March, in the third indiction, in the year 1185 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban III.

Place of the lead seal.

XXVI. He receives under protection the monastery of St. Saviour of Berardinga and confirms its possessions and privileges. (Verona, March 15.)

[Same work, p. 141.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons WILLIAM, abbot of St. Saviour of the Berardingi, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

[Col. 1375C] Apostolic protection ought to be present for those choosing the religious life, lest perhaps an assault of any rashness call them back from their purpose or—God forbid—break the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and, following the footsteps of Pope Alexander, our predecessor of happy memory, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the monastery of St. Saviour of the Berardingi, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing.

First, we decree that the monastic order known to have been established in the same place according to God, the Rule of blessed Benedict, and the order of the Camaldolese brethren shall be observed there inviolate for all time. Furthermore, whatever possessions or goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the Lord’s provision, through concessions of pontiffs, grants of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: the place itself in which the aforesaid monastery is situated, with its whole enclosure and all its appurtenances; the church of St. Martin beside the monastery; the church of St. Mary of Ripalta; the church of St. Bartholomew of Sextano; the church of St. Lawrence [Col. 1375D] of Quercitulo; the church of St. Paul above the river Bumba; the church of St. Christopher of Giustrigono; the church of St. Blaise of Cortina; the church of St. Michael of Casprino; the church of St. Lucy of Casprenello; the monastery of St. Vigilius in the city of Siena; the church of St. Christina in Luciniano Berardingo; the church of St. Martin of Picis; the church of St. Blaise of Palliario; the church of Saints Cosmas and Damian in Campis; the church of St. John of Arena; the church of Albert of holy memory on Mount Ilceto; and the church in the castle of Montirulo.

It shall also be lawful for you to receive clerics and laymen, free and absolved, who flee from the world to conversion, and to retain them without any opposition. [Col. 1376A] We forbid any of your brethren, after making profession in the same place, to leave your cloister through any levity without the permission of his abbot; and no one shall dare to retain one who has left without a letter of authorization from the community.

In the parish churches which you possess, it shall be lawful for you to choose priests and present them to the diocesan bishop. If they are found suitable, he shall commit the care of souls to them, so that they are bound to answer to him in spiritual matters and to you in temporal matters. When a general interdict of the land exists, it shall be lawful for you, with doors closed, bells not rung, excommunicated and interdicted persons excluded, and voices lowered, to celebrate the offices.

Furthermore, we grant that the burial place of that house shall be free [lacuna] their devotion and last will [lacuna] have resolved to be buried [lacuna] oppose; yet the right of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are brought shall be preserved.

No one shall presume to demand tithes from you on your newly cultivated lands, which you cultivate by your own hands or resources, or on the produce of [lacuna] your animals. Therefore we decree, etc.

Seal.

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Henry, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri, have subscribed. [Col. 1376D] I, John, cardinal priest of the title of St. Mark, have subscribed. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of St. Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the title of the Twelve Apostles, have subscribed. I, Albinus, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Melior, cardinal priest of the title of Pammachius of Saints John and Paul, have subscribed. I, Adelard, cardinal priest of the title of St. Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Soffredus, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. [Col. 1377A] I, Roland, cardinal deacon of St. Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Radulf, cardinal deacon of St. George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the Ides of March, in the third indiction, in the year 1185 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the first year of Pope Urban III.

XXVII. To (Hugh), abbot of Cluny, he affirms that the chaplaincy of the church of St. Vivien of Brollet, was granted by Adhemar, bishop of Saintes, to Theobald, “now bishop of Ostia and then abbot of Cluny.” (Verona, March 21.)

[*Bullarium Cluniacense*, p. 82.]

[Col. 1377B]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son the abbot of Cluny: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily grant assent to the just desires of petitioners, and bring to fulfilment, with the resulting effect, vows which do not depart from the path of reason. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, willingly concurring in your just petitions, we confirm by apostolic authority and strengthen by the protection of this present writing the chaplaincy of the church of St. Vivien of Brollet, with its appurtenances. Adhemar, bishop of Saintes, reasonably assigned it, with the consent of our beloved sons J., dean, R., archdeacon, and the canons of his church, to our venerable brother Theobald, now bishop of Ostia and then abbot of Cluny, and through him to his successors, so that he and each of his successors may possess it without dispute and may appoint a chaplain in that church, either personally or through his procurator.

We decree that no person at all may infringe this page of our confirmation or rashly act against it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of his blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

[Col. 1377D] Given at Verona, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of April.

XXVIII. To Gerard, archbishop of Ravenna, he affirms the procurations to be rendered by the monasteries of Bologna. (Verona, March 23.)

[MITTARELLI, *Annals of Camaldoli*, IV, appendix, p. 144.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother GERARD, archbishop of Ravenna: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We have seen the authentic instrument of Lucius, pope of happy memory, our father and predecessor, and from its tenor we have understood more fully that, when a controversy had long been pursued between you and the Bolognese monasteries, both of monks [Col. 1378A] and of nuns—except St. Bartholomew and St. Damian, which brought no complaint against you—concerning the procurations you demanded from them, he condemned the aforesaid monasteries, by common counsel of the brethren, to render procurations to you and your successors according to their means. Therefore, in order that this judgment may have greater permanence henceforth, we confirm it by apostolic authority, as it is contained in the authentic instrument. For greater clarity, we have thought fit to set out that instrument word for word:

LUCIUS, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother GERARD, archbishop of Ravenna: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1378B] Disputes settled by judgment of the Apostolic See are committed to writing for perpetual remembrance, lest in the course of time they be capable of being revived through forgetfulness. So that the judgment may have greater force, it is strengthened by the protection of an apostolic writing.

Now, when a controversy concerning the procurations which you demanded from them was pending between you and the Bolognese monasteries, both of monks and of nuns, we committed it to our venerable brother Henry, bishop of Albano, for hearing. Subsequently our beloved son, the abbot of St. Proculus, procurator of all the others, as appeared from the letters which he produced and as he himself confirmed by pledge given into the hand of the said bishop, litigated at length before us and our brethren on his own behalf and that of the others—except St. Bartholomew and St. Damian, [Col. 1378C] which made no complaint on this question.

Yet on his side he produced no privileges of the Roman or Ravennate Church, nor did he show himself supported by long custom. But you proved through suitable witnesses that these procurations are rendered without objection in the other monasteries of your province, and that they had been rendered to your predecessors in the monasteries of the city of Bologna. Consequently, after deliberation with our brethren, we saw that your claim was supported by common law and by the custom of your predecessors.

Therefore, assenting to your just petitions, by common counsel of the brethren we condemned the aforesaid monasteries to render procurations according to their means to you and your successors; and, adjudging them to you in all the aforesaid monasteries, we have caused the judgment which we pronounced to be strengthened by our subscriptions and those of the brethren. Therefore we decree that no one, etc.

Seal.

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Henry, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri, have subscribed. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark, have subscribed. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Calixtus, have subscribed. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the title of the Twelve Apostles, have subscribed. [Col. 1379A] I, Melior, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius, have subscribed. I, Adelard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Soffredus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Roland, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Radulf, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, [Col. 1379B] on the tenth day before the Kalends of April [23 March], in the fourth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1185, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban III.

The holes of the lost seal are visible.

### XXIX. He decrees “that no prelates shall presume to demand procurations from the priories of the monastery of Cluny except when they are present there.”  
*(Verona, 25 March.)*

*[Bullarium Cluniacense, p. 83.]*

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot and convent of Cluny: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The more greatly your monastery has long flourished in religious life, [Col. 1379C] and the more persons have, by your example, devoted themselves to the service of the Creator, the more closely ought we to love you and your monastery in charity, and to defend you more earnestly from the burdens imposed by anyone whatsoever. Yet, as has been reported to our ears on your behalf, certain prelates of churches, who by custom ought to be provided with procurations by your priories, often demand that procurations be supplied to them elsewhere, in certain small towns, although they do not at all come to the priories themselves. They have not been accustomed to do this, and their wishes in this matter cannot be satisfied without more serious expense to those priories.

Therefore, wishing to provide against your burden in this respect, by the authority of this present document we forbid any prelates maliciously to presume, contrary to [Col. 1379D] ancient custom, to demand or extort procurations outside your priories from those priories. Let no person whatsoever, therefore, be permitted to infringe this document of our prohibition or rashly to oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, on the eighth day before the Kalends of April [25 March].

### XXX. At the request of Abbot Hugh, he confirms the possessions and privileges of the monastery of Cluny.  
*(Verona, 2 April.)*

*[Ibid., p. 83.]*

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1380A] sons HUGH, abbot of the monastery of Cluny, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

The monastery of Cluny, a mirror of monastic religious life in modern times and an example in the regions of Gaul, was, from the very beginning of its foundation, offered to the Apostolic See as its own possession. Accordingly, our predecessors of holy memory—John XI, likewise John XIX, Agapetus II, Benedict VI; likewise Benedict VII, Leo VII; likewise Leo IX, Gregory VI; likewise Gregory VII, Alexander II, Stephen, Victor III, Urban II, Paschal II, Gelasius II, Calixtus II, Honorius II, and Eugenius, Roman pontiffs—endowed that place with the prerogative of singular affection and freedom, [Col. 1380B] and fortified all its appurtenances by the enactments of their privileges.

For it has been established that all churches, cemeteries, monks, clerics, and all laypersons dwelling within the boundaries—which run from the stream of Salnay, and from the church of Ruffiac, and the cross of Lornant, also from the boundary of the mill of Fornescach, through the village called Varenna, together with the wood of Burserius and the boundary likewise called Perois, as far as the stream of Salnay—shall remain solely under the jurisdiction and protection of the Apostolic See. Nor are the priests or parishioners of the place of Cluny itself to be compelled to attend any synod or assembly except that of the Roman pontiff and the abbot of Cluny.

Moreover, for the ordination of an abbot, monks, or clerics dwelling within the aforesaid boundaries; for the preparation of chrism; and for the consecration of holy oil, altars, and cemeteries, the monastery of Cluny may summon whichever bishop it prefers. No person whatsoever, except the Roman pontiff and a legate dispatched for this purpose from his side, may excommunicate or place under interdict Cluniac monks dwelling anywhere. Moreover, we confirm by this present decree the boundaries of immunity of your place, established by our aforesaid predecessor Pope Urban: namely, that no person, of whatever rank or power, may presume to commit invasion, plunder, or robbery, or to perpetrate homicide within the limits of those boundaries.

Accordingly, these are the boundaries of the sacred ban: toward Buziacum, [Col. 1380D] the boundary is at Rivium on this side of Sarrata, whence one road goes to Cluny and another to Mâcon. On the highway toward Beaujeu, the boundary is opposite Carruvium, which lies above the mill of the cellarer of Cluny, on this side of Viengias beyond Cluny. Toward Mâcon, the boundary is at the crossroads, whence one road leads to Mâcon and another to Saint Mary of the Wood. Above Ruffiac, the boundary is at the summit of the protected enclosure, at the crossroads whence one road leads to Bezornyacum and another to Carella. Toward Sergiacum, the boundary is within Guarruvium, on this side of the place called *ad Furgum*. On the highway toward the district of Chalon, the boundary is at the Great Oak above Marziacum. [Col. 1381A] Toward Brancedunum, the boundary is on the road above Boscus Bannedus. Toward Trinorchium, it is above the stream called Long Water, between Blanoscus and Donziacum. Toward Perrona or Laysiacum, the boundary is at the three beeches, where the wood of Cluny and the wood of the county are divided. Toward Igiacum, it is at Carmos on the middle mountain.

In the abbeys which, together with their abbots, have been given into the governance of the monastery of Cluny—namely, Saint Martial of Limoges; the New Monastery at Poitiers; Saint John of Angély; the monastery of Lézat; Moissac; Figeac, in the district of Cahors; in Auvergne, Mozac, Thiers, and Menat; in the diocese of Auxerre, Saint Germanus; in the diocese of Rouen, [Col. 1381B] the abbey at Pontoise; and in the diocese of Thérouanne, Saint Wulmar—an abbot is in no way to be elected without the counsel of the abbot of Cluny.

To this we add that in all priories and cells now subject to your governance without an abbot of their own, no one shall ever presume in future times to appoint an abbot. Rather, both those priories and cells, and likewise all other things in whatsoever places with which the Church of Cluny was invested at the time of the council of Auvergne held by the aforesaid Pope Urban, and concerning which no dispute was then raised, shall always be preserved to you and to your successors in peace and tranquillity.

No bishop may have power to inflict upon you any burden or annoyance concerning your altars, churches, or tithes; but, just as you held some of these in part and some wholly by their permission, so shall you hold them in the future. You may possess, for your own governance and that of the poor, the tithes of your churches which are held by laymen, if reverence for your religious order can, in accordance with God, withdraw them from those persons’ control. You shall henceforth more peacefully possess, without any opposition from bishops or episcopal officials, the tithes of your labour—namely, of those lands which they call *dominicaturae*, cultivated at your expense by the dependants of your monastery and cells—for which bishops have been accustomed to trouble both you and other men of the monastic order; for you distribute these tithes [Col. 1381D] to travelling brethren and the poor.

All your churches, wherever located, and your chapels and cemeteries, shall be free and exempt from every exaction, except for the customary share of the bishop and his jurisdiction over priests who offend against the dignity of their order. You or your brethren may also choose priests for your churches, provided that they receive the care of souls from bishops or the bishops’ vicars without simony. If, God forbid, the latter should perversely refuse to confer it, then the priests shall obtain, through the benevolence of the Apostolic See, permission to celebrate the offices. If diocesan bishops are unwilling to provide freely the consecration of churches or altars, receive it from any Catholic bishop whom you choose. Nor shall the brethren of your cells, wherever situated, suffer suspension of divine offices on account of any interdict or excommunication; rather, both the monks themselves and their servants, and those who have vowed themselves to the monastic profession, shall celebrate the offices of divine service and perform the rites due for burial behind closed church doors, admitting no diocesan officials.

Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire, God granting, by concession of popes, gift of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. We have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names: in Burgundy, the church of Villefranche, the church of Balberiacum, [Col. 1382B] the monastery of Prims, the monastery of Saint John of the Wood, and the monastery at Beaune, built by you from the alms of the duke of Burgundy. In France, the monastery of Montdésir, the monastery of Domna Petra, and the monastery of Saint Arnulf of Crispeium. In the diocese of Cambrai, the monastery of Saint Salvius; in Provence, the monastery near the mountain of Montpellier and the monastery of Tornac; in the diocese of Toulouse, the church of Saint Columba. In Spain: Nazara, Saint Isidore, Saint Zoilus of Carrión, Saint Romanus of Peñas, Villaverde, Villafranca, Valleverde, Palumbarium Bodinum, Viminaria, Saint Martin of Nebda, Saint Vincent of Salamanca, Saint Columba of Burgos, [Col. 1382C] and Cornilana, which have been assigned specifically to the monastery of Cluny. Likewise, in the diocese of Nevers, the monastery of Albaniacum, which belongs to La Charité. In France, the monastery of Causiacum, which belongs to Saint Martin-des-Champs; the canonical church of Abbeville; likewise the church of Rue, which belongs to the monastery of Abbeville.

We forbid anyone to presume to build a church or chapel within parishes belonging to the jurisdiction of the monastery of Cluny without the consent of the abbot of Cluny, with the authority of the Apostolic See reserved in all things. We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass them with any vexations whatsoever; rather, everything shall be preserved intact for the benefit in every respect of those for whose governance and support it was granted. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, etc., as in the other documents.

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Henry, bishop of Albano. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Calixtus. [Col. 1383A] I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the title of the Twelve Apostles. I, Albinus, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Melior, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. I, Adelard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, Solfredus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Radulf, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman [Col. 1383B] Church, on the fourth day before the Nones of April [2 April], in the fourth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1186, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban III.

### XXXI. He receives the monastery of Tegernsee under protection and confirms its possessions.  
*(Verona, 2 April.)*

*[Monumenta Boica, VI, 189.]*

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ROUPERT, abbot of the monastery of Saint Quirinus near Lake Tegernsee, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

[Col. 1383C] Apostolic protection ought to be available to those choosing the religious life, lest perhaps an attack of any rashness either draw them back from their purpose or, which God forbid, weaken the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, after the example of our predecessor Pope Alexander of happy memory, and strengthen by the privilege of this present document, the aforesaid monastery of Saint Quirinus. It was built upon their own estate by the noblemen Adalbert and Otkar, brothers and illustrious counts; it was endowed with the ancient privileges of the Roman emperors—namely, Pippin, Charles, and Louis; and in it, it is reported, rests the body of blessed Quirinus, obtained from our predecessor of holy memory Zachary, Roman pontiff.

First, indeed, we establish that the monastic order known to have been instituted in that place according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict shall there be observed inviolate in perpetuity. Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire, the Lord providing, by concession of popes, gift of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. We have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

[Col. 1384A] The place itself in which the aforesaid monastery is situated, with all its appurtenances; the cell of blessed Martin, called Dietramszelle; the churches of Gemunden, Egerden, Wacchergen, Rihherspowern, Waringew, Walde, Harpenningen, Holzchirchen, Pousenchaim, Pipurch, Hadelahingen, Harde, Ismpach, Chemenaten, Munchen, Charidewe, Phrumpach, Waterstetm, Walhstat, Itihingen, Uneholzingen, Chenepah, and Funsingen, with their estates, adjacent lands, and people.

Furthermore, we likewise confirm to you the liberties or immunities reasonably granted to your monastery and confirmed in writing by archbishops, bishops, kings, and princes; and by apostolic authority we forbid anyone to infringe or enfeoff them. [Col. 1384B] Moreover, we prohibit any archbishop or bishop from granting churches belonging to your monastery to anyone without your consent. Rather, you may present priests to bishops for vacant churches; if they are suitable, the bishops shall confer the care of souls upon them without abuse, with the constitution of the Lateran Council reserved; provided that they owe obedience to the bishops in spiritual matters and to you in temporal matters.

Likewise, we forbid any archbishop, bishop, or other ecclesiastical person to subject you or your monastery to excommunication or interdict without a manifest and reasonable cause. When there is a general interdict of the land, you may celebrate divine offices behind closed doors, excluding excommunicated and interdicted persons, without ringing bells and in a subdued voice. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars or churches, and the ordination of monks or clerics to be promoted to holy orders from the diocesan bishop, if he is Catholic, enjoys the favour and communion of the Apostolic See, and is willing to provide these to you freely and without abuse. Otherwise, you may approach whichever Catholic bishop you choose; supported by our authority, he shall undoubtedly grant what is requested.

Furthermore, wishing, son abbot, to honour you and your church with a special privilege after the example of our aforesaid predecessor, we grant to you and [Col. 1384D] your successors, out of the customary clemency and apostolic benevolence of the Apostolic See, the use of the mitre and ring at the principal solemnities during the solemnities of Mass, in the processions of your church, and also in councils of bishops, so that by this you may remain more devoted to blessed Peter and to us.

When you, the present abbot of that place, or any of your successors dies, no one shall be set over it by any artifice of deceit or violence, except the man whom the brethren by common consent, or the sounder counsel of the brethren, shall judge to be elected according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict.

We decree, therefore, etc. But to all who preserve the rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action [Col. 1385A] and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Henry, bishop of Albano. I, Tebaud, bishop of Ostia and Velletri, etc.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the third day before the Nones of April [3 April], in the fourth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1186, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban III.

### XXXII. He forbids archbishops and bishops “henceforth to require any procurations from the Cluniac brethren unless they have come to their priories for visitation.”  
*(Verona, 5 April.)*

*[Bullarium Cluniacense, p. 8.]*

[Col. 1385B]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren the archbishops and bishops in whose parishes the priories and obediences of the Church of Cluny are situated: greeting and apostolic blessing.

By divine ordinance, prelates of churches are permitted, while sowing spiritual things, to reap and receive temporal things, according to the saying: “You shall not muzzle an ox while it is treading grain,” so that they may not be a burden to the churches entrusted to them. But we have learned that some of you, not attending to this as you ought, [Col. 1385C] when you travel about your dioceses, cause procurations to be supplied to you by the priories and obediences of the Cluniac brethren while you are lodged elsewhere, although, as they assert, they were ready to receive you kindly in their own priories and to serve you with eager devotion.

Since it is unworthy, and alike contrary to your honour, to turn the services of ecclesiastical charity into a burden upon subjects, by the authority of the present document we strictly forbid your fraternity henceforth, unless you have come to the aforesaid brethren’s priories for the purpose of visitation, to require any procurations from them or to inflict upon them any burden or annoyance on this account. Know that, if you act otherwise, we shall, the Lord being the author, take care to forbid those brethren to furnish procuration to you when you are lodged [Col. 1385D] elsewhere.

Given at Verona, on the Nones of April [5 April].

### XXXIII. He receives the monastery of Roche under protection and confirms its possessions.  
*(Verona, 7 April.)*

*[Monasticon Anglicanum, I, 839.]*

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons OSMUND, abbot of Roche, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: greeting in Christ.

Apostolic protection ought to be available to those choosing the religious life, lest perhaps an attack of any rashness either draw them back from their purpose or, which God forbid, weaken the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, [Col. 1386A] beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, and after the example of our predecessor Pope Lucius of happy memory, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and strengthen by the privilege of this present document, the aforesaid monastery of Roche, in which you are devoted to divine service.

First, indeed, we establish that the monastic order known to have been instituted in that monastery according to the Lord, the Rule of blessed Benedict, and the institution of the Cistercian brethren shall there be observed inviolate in perpetuity. Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire, the Lord providing, by concession of popes, gift of kings [Col. 1386B] or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. We have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

By the gift of Richard de Builli and Richard de Wikerestai, the place itself on which your abbey stands. By the gift of Lord King Henry II, one hundred acres in Lyndrie, near the same abbey. By the gift of the same persons, the grange of Aggacroft with its appurtenances. By the gift of the same Richard de Builli and Hugh de Drigwrt, Lambecroft with its appurtenances. By the gift of Leo de Manners, Brantecliva with its appurtenances. By the gift of Ralph Tortesmanse, Tatewit [Col. 1386C] with its appurtenances. By the gift of William Avenell, Anes [lacuna] with its appurtenances. By the gift of Walter de Scoteni, Rokesbye with its appurtenances. By the gift of Simon son of Simon, land in Inssebye with its appurtenances. By the gift of Hamelin Bardoufe and Robert son of Eudo, the land of Wintrington with its appurtenances. By the gift of Robert de Scalcebye, Adam de Novo-foro, and Roger de Yar, Newsum with its appurtenances. By the gift of William Vavassor, Tirnesco with its appurtenances. By the gift of Gervase de Barneby, the grange at Barneby and Brawith. By the gift of Thomas de Arneltorp, a grange in the same village. By the gift of Robert son of Pagan, Wellingleia with its appurtenances, and all the land which you hold in the territory of Wadburthe. By the gift of William [Col. 1386D] de Poles and William son of Gerard, Sezacres with its appurtenances. By the gift of Simon de Plessai, Ashoure with its appurtenances. By the gift of Robert son of Glai, land and wood from Cumresbruig as far as Witewelle, between the road and the stream. By the gift of William Flandrigene, all the land which Ligulf held, and a certain clearing belonging to him, which lies between Hestvelle and the clearing of Orm, a man of Adam son of Swani, with all appurtenances. By the gift of Gerard de Stirap, a certain peat-bog in the territory of the same village.

Moreover, let no one presume to demand or extort tithes from you on the produce which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, whether from cultivated or uncultivated lands or from the increase of your animals, etc.

[Col. 1387A] Given at Verona, through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Ides of April [7 April], in the fourth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1186; in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban III.

### XXXIV. Fragment of a privilege for the Church of Ravenna.  
*(Verona, 8 April.)*

*[Rubeus, History of Ravenna, pp. 357–58.]*

Urban III, by letters given at Verona on the fifth day before the Ides of April [9 April], granted Gerard, archbishop of Ravenna, that, with the consent of the sacred ministers of this church, he might alienate possessions of the Church of Ravenna which were far away and less useful, such as those at Pula and in certain other [Col. 1387B] places; provided, however, that he made provision for what was better for the Church, and applied to its benefit whatever money he should obtain from them. This is the beginning of those letters:

“Since, by God’s favour, many benefits have accrued to the church entrusted to you through your diligence, and you have taken care no less to benefit it than to preside over it hitherto, we hold without doubt that you ought to provide for its future advantage.”

### XXXV. Privilege for the hospitaller house of the brethren of the Cross-bearers of Saint Peter of Boica.  
*(Verona, 8 May.)*

*[Farlatus, Illyricum Sacrum, IV, 216.]*

[Col. 1387C]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons MATTHEW, rector, and the Cross-bearing brethren of the hospital of Saint Peter of Boica, present and future, living the common life: for perpetual remembrance.

To grant effect to just petitioners is required both by the force of equity and by the order of reason, especially when piety supports the petitioners’ wish and truth does not abandon it. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves, and strengthen by the privilege of this present document, the aforesaid hospital of Saint Peter of Boisce, together with all that it now justly and canonically possesses or may in future acquire, [Col. 1387D] the Lord providing, by concession of popes, gift of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other just means. We establish that these shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors.

We have thought fit to specify these possessions by their proper names: the place itself in which the aforesaid hospital is situated, with all its appurtenances; the church of Boisce, situated in the regions of Slavonia, which the bishop of Nin reasonably assigned to your order, as is fully contained in his own authenticated document to you—we confirm it to you and your successors by apostolic authority—and whatever you possess in the place called Palatium. Moreover, no one may presume to demand or extort tithes from you on your newly cultivated lands, which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or on the increase of your animals. [Col. 1388A] You may also receive into your conversion clerics or laymen fleeing the world, free and unencumbered, and retain them without any opposition.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid hospital, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass them by any vexations whatsoever; rather, everything shall be preserved intact for the benefit in every respect of those for whose support and governance it was granted, with the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical jurisdiction of the diocesan bishop reserved.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future knowingly attempts rashly to act against this document of our enactment, and, having been warned a second or third time, does not correct and amend the wrong committed by suitable satisfaction, let that person be deprived of the rank of his power and honour; let him know that he stands guilty before divine judgement for the iniquity perpetrated; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and Lord, our Redeemer Jesus Christ; and at the last judgement let him be subject to strict vengeance. But to all who preserve the rights of that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict judge [Col. 1388C] the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Henry, bishop of Albano. I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, John, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Mark. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Calixtus. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the Twelve Apostles. I, Albinus, cardinal priest of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem. I, Melior, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, [Col. 1388D] of the title of Pammachius. I, Adelard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, James, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Bobo, cardinal deacon of Saint Angelus. I, Octavian, cardinal deacon of Saints Sergius and Bacchus. I, Goffredus, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Ides of May [8 May], in the fourth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1186, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban III.

### XXXVI. He receives the monastery of Vallombrosa under protection and confirms its possessions and rights.  
*(Verona, 12 May.)*

*[Lami, Ecclesiastical Monuments of Florence, I, 548.]*

[Col. 1389A]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons TERTIUS, abbot of Vallombrosa, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

Apostolic protection ought to be available to those choosing the religious life, lest perhaps an attack of any rashness draw them back from their purpose or, which God forbid, weaken the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, and receive the monastery of Vallombrosa, [Col. 1389B] in which you are devoted to divine service, into the ownership of the Roman Church, the guardianship, and the protection of the Apostolic See, in honour of the blessed Virgin Mary, to whom it is dedicated to God; following the example of Paschal, Adrian, Alexander, and Lucius, Roman pontiffs of happy memory, we strengthen it by the privilege of this present document.

First, indeed, we establish that the monastic order known to have been instituted in that place according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict shall there be observed inviolate in perpetuity. Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire, the Lord providing, by concession of popes, gift of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, [Col. 1389C] or other just means, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. We have thought fit to specify the following by their proper names:

The place itself in which the aforesaid monastery is situated, with all its adjacent lands and appurtenances, churches, and other things known to belong to that monastery; the monastery of Saint Salvius; the monastery of the Holy Trinity of Florence; the monastery of Struma; the monastery of Osella and Saint James of the Castle; the monastery of Passignano, and of Saint Michael of Siena and of Alfiano; the monastery of Cultubono, of Monte Pisano; the monastery of Monte Scalario and of Nerano; the monastery of Ficiclo; [Col. 1389D] the monastery of Capiano; the monastery of Saint Paul of Pisa, and of Saint Michael of Plajano, and of Saint Michael of Salvenere in Sardinia; the monastery of Saint Angelus of Pistoia; the monastery of Pacciano; the monastery of Saint Mary of Prato; the monastery of Vaiano; the monastery of Appleto and of Monte Plano; the monastery of Fonte Thaonis; the monastery of Musceto; the monastery of Monte Armato; the monastery of Saint Cecilia; the monastery of Saint Reparata; the monastery of Trecento; the monastery of Crispino; the monastery of Razzolo; the monastery of the Holy Sepulchre of Pavia; the monastery of Rivo Caesaris; the monastery of Coneo; the monastery of Turri; the monastery of Caprilia; the monastery of Saint Benedict of Piacenza. The monastery of Cavanna; [Col. 1390A] the monastery of Saint Mercurialis of Forlì; the monastery of Navaria; the monastery of Vercelli; the monastery of Genoa; the monastery of Saint Paul of Tortona; the monastery of Turin; the monastery of Brescia; the monastery of Saint Vigilius; the monastery of Bergamo; the monastery of Milan and Saint Carpophorus; the monastery of Asti; the monastery of Saint Angelus of Juniperitum; the monastery of Saint Sigismund; and the monastery of Saint Mary of Flumana.

We hold valid, and confirm by apostolic authority, the liberties and immunities granted to you by our predecessors of happy memory—Victor, Gregory VII, Urban II, Paschal, Innocent, Eugenius, Alexander, and Lucius, Roman pontiffs—and peaceably preserved until these times. [Col. 1390B] Moreover, we decree that the tithes of your produce, which you gather anywhere by your own expense and labour, shall be rendered to and possessed by your monastery without opposition from bishops, episcopal officials, or parish priests.

It shall also be lawful for you to receive for conversion clerics or laymen fleeing from the world, free and absolved, and to retain them without any opposition. Nor may anyone remove and transfer any monastery of your religious order from the stability of its site without the common consent of the abbot and community. Moreover, we decree that no bishop may lawfully pronounce upon you a sentence of excommunication or interdict, so that, having been received as special sons of the apostolic see, you may be subject to the judgment of no other. [Col. 1390C] We establish that the monastery situated at Vallombrosa shall be regarded as the head of all the aforesaid monasteries. Indeed, when the end of life comes to your pastor by divine dispensation, the person to be appointed in his place, since he must preside over you and all the others, shall be elected by the consent and decision of all those who preside over the other monasteries. But if, by the Lord’s ordering, any one of those abbots should be elected to this general governance, he shall proceed to your principal monastery; and thereafter, by his judgment, as is known to have been done in the days of John, your first abbot of venerable memory, all the other monasteries united to you shall be governed. We also grant you free burial, [Col. 1390D] so that no one may oppose the devotion and final wish of those who decide to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or under interdict, while preserving nevertheless the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken. You shall receive chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars or churches, and the ordination of your clerics and monks from whichever bishop you prefer, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the grace and communion of the apostolic see, and is willing to confer these things freely and without any improper charge.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, remove its possessions, retain possessions taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things [Col. 1391A] shall be preserved unimpaired and whole, for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the apostolic see. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this charter of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, having been warned a second or third time, unless he correct his offense by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance.

But upon all who preserve the rights of that place, [Col. 1391B] may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that they may receive here the fruit of good conduct and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Henry, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri, have subscribed. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Mark, have subscribed. I, Peter, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Susanna, have subscribed. I, Laborans, priest-cardinal of St. Mary across the Tiber, of the title of St. Callistus, have subscribed. [Col. 1391C] I, Albinus, priest-cardinal of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Melior, priest-cardinal of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius, have subscribed. I, Adelard, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Marcellus, have subscribed. I, James, deacon-cardinal of St. Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed. I, Gratian, deacon-cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Bobo, deacon-cardinal of St. Angelo, have subscribed. I, Peter, deacon-cardinal of St. Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Rodolph, deacon-cardinal of St. George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

[Col. 1391D] Given at Verona through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth Ides of May, in the fourth indiction, in the year of the Lord’s Incarnation 1186, in the first year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban III.

### XXXVII. Privilege for the monastery of St. Saviour at Pavia.  
*(Verona, 22 May.)*

[Margarini, *Bullar. Casin.*, II, 209.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son LEO, abbot of the monastery of St. Saviour situated near Pavia, and to his successors professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

For those choosing the religious life, apostolic protection ought to be at hand, lest perhaps an assault of any rashness [Col. 1392A] either turn them from their purpose or—God forbid—weaken the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and, following the example of John, Benedict, Eugenius, and other Roman pontiffs of blessed memory, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery of St. Saviour, in which you are dedicated to the service of the Lord, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present document. First, indeed, we establish that the monastic order known to have been instituted in that place according to God and the Rule of St. Benedict shall be observed there inviolably for all time.

Furthermore, whatever possessions and goods that monastery now [Col. 1392B] justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of popes, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, through the Lord’s favor, shall remain secure and unimpaired to you and your successors. Among these we have thought it proper to specify the following by their own names:

The site itself upon which the aforesaid monastery stands, with all its appurtenances; the estate of Olona, with the chapel of St. Anastasius and the chapel of St. Stephen the protomartyr; the chapel of St. George, with all belonging to it; the estate of Baseregutia, with the baptismal church of St. Andrew built there, one chapel, and all its appurtenances; [Col. 1392C] the estate of Frisinaria, with one chapel and all its appurtenances; the estate of Mellaria, with the parish church of St. Michael, the cell of St. Stephen, the chapel of St. Martin, and all appurtenances; one half of the estate of Herberia, and the parish church of St. Faustinus with all that belongs to that half and parish church; in whose parish and territory are three chapels, namely those of St. Michael, St. Fabian, and St. Agatha; the orchard situated within St. John’s Gate near the Palatine Gate, with two chapels, one built in honor of St. Lawrence and the other in honor of St. Mary; the estate of Garlasco, with one chapel of St. Mary and with every honor and jurisdiction for two miles around; at Morinco, a parish church in honor of St. [Col. 1392D] Martin and a chapel built in honor of St. Mary, with all their appurtenances; the estate of Blondo, with two chapels and all its appurtenances; the estate of Cocomato, with all its appurtenances; the estate of Mociano, with all its appurtenances; one half of the estate of Coriana, with a chapel in honor of St. Mary and with the jurisdiction of the whole aforesaid estate; the estate of Antellami, with all appurtenances; the estate of Armentarii, with one chapel and all its appurtenances; at Rongaria, the chapel of St. Maurice.

Indeed, let no one presume to demand or extort from you tithes of your newly cleared lands (*novalia*) which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the produce of your animals. When, however, a general interdict of the land has been imposed, it shall be lawful for you, with doors shut, excommunicated and interdicted persons excluded, bells not rung, and voices lowered, to celebrate the divine offices. [Col. 1393A] Furthermore, we wholly prohibit new and undue exactions by archbishops, bishops, archdeacons, deacons, and all other ecclesiastical or secular persons. We also decree by this present ordinance that the liberties and immunities granted to the same monastery by kings and princes especially, and by other persons, both ecclesiastical and secular, together with its ancient and reasonable customs, shall remain whole and unimpaired.

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, the consecration of altars or churches, and the ordination of monks, canons, or those to be promoted to sacred orders from whichever [Col. 1393B] bishop you prefer, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the grace and communion of the apostolic see, and is willing to provide these things freely and without any improper charge. Furthermore, in churches belonging to the same monastery—namely, the church of St. Martin of Morinco, the church of St. Faustinus of Herbaria, the church of St. Michael of Mellaria, the church of St. Anastasius of Olona, and the church of St. Saviour of Monticelli—we grant by apostolic authority the right of baptism; likewise in the other churches belonging to that monastery where baptism is known to have been celebrated until the present time. We also grant you the use of stockings, sandals, gloves, and mitre, as is known to have been granted to you and your successors by the authoritative privileges [Col. 1393C] of our predecessors, and as we now grant to you from the liberality of the apostolic see.

In addition, we add in this present chapter that the aforesaid monastery, with all the things stated above, shall remain subject to the jurisdiction of no church, but shall be answerable to the holy apostolic see alone. On your death, as abbot of that place, no one shall be placed over it by any cunning of intrusion or by force, except one whom the brethren, by common consent or the sounder part of the council, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of St. Benedict, have judged ought to be elected. The person elected shall come to the Roman pontiff to receive blessing.

We therefore decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery or [Col. 1393D] remove its possessions, retain possessions removed, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things shall be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those for whose governance and support they were granted, saving in all things the authority of the apostolic see. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this charter of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, then, having been warned a second or third time, unless he correct his offense by suitable satisfaction, let him lose the dignity of his power and honor; let him know himself guilty before divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be separated from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. [Col. 1394A] But upon all who preserve their rights to that place, may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that they may receive here the fruit of good conduct and, before the strict Judge, find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia, have subscribed. I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Henry, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, John, priest-cardinal of the title church of St. Mark, have subscribed. I, Peter de Bono, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Susanna, have subscribed. I, Laborans, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Mary across the Tiber, have subscribed. I, Pandulph, priest-cardinal of the title of the Basilica [Col. 1394B] of the Twelve Apostles, have subscribed. I, Albert, priest-cardinal of the title of Holy Cross in Jerusalem, have subscribed. I, Melior, priest-cardinal of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius, have subscribed. I, Adelard, priest-cardinal of the title of St. Marcellus, have subscribed.
