It is fitting that we readily grant assent to the just desires of petitioners, and bring to fulfilment the prayers which do not depart from the path of reason. Therefore, with grateful assent to your just requests, by authority of these present letters we decree that whatever has been lawfully granted to you through the donation and devotion of emperors, kings, or other princes—whether in possessions, dignities, or other things—shall remain firm and inviolate for you and your successors. Under threat of anathema we forbid anyone rashly to take them away, disturb them, or retain them to your prejudice. We decree, therefore, [Col. 1474B] etc.

Given at Verona, the tenth day before the Kalends of April [23 March].

LXXXVI. Bull for the canons of Modena. (Verona, 5 April.)

[TIRABOSCHI, *Memorie Modenesi*, III, 99.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Master Martin, provost, and the canons of Modena: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Measures prudently established for preserving an institution’s condition ought to stand firm and inviolate and, lest they be violated through anyone’s malice, should be secured by apostolic writings. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, yielding to your requests, we decree to be valid and firm the arrangement prudently made between you and H., bishop of Modena of happy memory, with the assent and approval of M., cardinal-deacon of St George at the Golden Veil, of happy memory, then legate of the Apostolic See, concerning the reception of legates of the Roman Church and provision for the archbishop of Ravenna: namely, that whether your bishop is absent or present, he is bound to provide the whole provision for the first day, while you are bound to provide the whole of the second day for the said archbishop and legates. This arrangement was prudently made and accepted by consent of the parties, and subsequently confirmed in apostolic letters by Alexander, our predecessor of happy memory; we secure it by the protection of this writing. [Col. 1474D] Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe this page of our confirmation or, with rash presumption, oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, on the Nones of April [5 April].

LXXXVII. He confirms the possessions of P., provost of Reggio. (Verona, 9 April.)

[Same work, p. 100.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son P., provost of Reggio: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The most holy Roman Church, in the office of its customary mercy, is accustomed to embrace with particular affection its devoted and humble [Col. 1475A] sons, and to foster them by the protection of its safeguard, lest they suffer the vexation of wicked persons [lacuna]. Therefore, beloved son in Christ, considering the devotion which you are known to have toward blessed Peter and ourselves, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves your person, together with all the ecclesiastical and temporal goods which you now rightfully and peacefully possess or may hereafter, by God’s aid, acquire through lawful means.

In particular, we confirm to your devotion by apostolic authority the church of St Mary of Fabrica, which you acquired through the election of its brethren, with the consent of the canons of the Church of Reggio and by the grant of our venerable brother, the bishop of Reggio, long before the death of Pope Alexander, our predecessor of happy memory, and which you now possess without dispute; and we strengthen it by the protection of this writing. Therefore let no one, etc.

Given at Verona, on the Ides of April [13 April].

LXXXVIII. He appoints Henry, archbishop of Bourges, his legate throughout the province of Bourges, excepting the monastery of Dol. (Verona, 13 April.)

[*Gallia Christiana*, new edition, II, Documents, p. 18.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brothers the bishops, to his beloved sons the abbots and other prelates of churches, and to all clergy and people established throughout the province of Bourges: greeting [Col. 1475C] and apostolic blessing.

Since, in consideration of the benefits which we long ago received from the Church of Bourges while holding a lesser office, we are bound to love it in particular and above other churches of Gaul, we willingly wish, as is fitting, to honour it with the prerogative of our affection and favour. Moreover, the proved devotion of our venerable brother Henry, archbishop of that same church, moves us to extend more abundantly to it the favour of the Apostolic See. For we know him, a prudent and discerning man, noble in character and birth, to have displayed toward us and the Roman Church such devotion that, his merits supporting him, he ought to be loved more warmly and honoured more attentively by the Apostolic See.

Accordingly, having weighed his prudence and integrity, with the counsel of our brothers we have entrusted to him throughout your province—excepting the monastery of Dol—the office of apostolic legation, to be exercised in our stead: that he may correct what needs correction, plant what he knows ought to be planted, and, having uprooted vices, strive to foster the shoots of virtues. Therefore we command and enjoin all of you to take care reverently and devoutly to receive this archbishop as legate of the Apostolic See and as a man of such dignity and reputation; to come at his summons without any opposition; and humbly to obey his wholesome statutes and commands. Thus, through his prudence and your humility, he may more effectively discharge [Col. 1476A] the office of legation entrusted to him with the aid of heavenly grace, and, when we hear of it, we may deservedly commend your devotion and obedience.

Given at Verona, on the Ides of April [13 April].

LXXXIX. He affirms for the Carthusian brothers the free right to elect their prior and procurator. (Verona, 18 April.)

[*Privileges of the Carthusian Order*, fol. 2r.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the prior and Carthusian brothers: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The more worthy the service rendered to the Lord in religious places, the more closely we ought to embrace them in affection and the more carefully to attend to their welfare. Therefore, wishing to provide for your interests with paternal concern, by the authority of these present letters we have judged it necessary to forbid that any prior or procurator be set over the same house through anyone’s force or guile, except one whom the brothers, by common counsel or by the counsel of the greater and sounder part, shall judge to be elected according to the statutes of the order.

Given at Verona, the fourteenth day before the Kalends of May [18 April].

XC. He grants to Michael, abbot of the monastery of St Peter of Modena, and to his successors the use of the mitre, sandals, stockings, and gloves. (Verona, 26 April.)

[TIRABOSCHI, *Memorie Modenesi*, III, 100.]

[Col. 1476C]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son Michael, abbot of St Peter, situated near the city of Modena: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The Roman Church is accustomed to embrace with affection those whose devotion it has experienced in many ways. Induced by this consideration, and likewise moved by your requests, on account of that charity with which, while we held a lesser office, we embraced you and your church, we grant to you and your successors the use of the mitre, sandals, stockings, and gloves; and, just as you and your predecessors are known to have possessed them for the past forty years, we confirm this by the page of the present writing. [Col. 1476D] Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe this page of our grant and confirmation or, with rash presumption, oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, the sixth day before the Kalends of May [26 April].

XCI. Privilege for the church of St Salvius at Florence. (Verona, 4 May.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, III, 99.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Gilbert, abbot, and the convent of St Salvius of Florence: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1477A] It is fitting that we readily grant assent to the just desires of petitioners, and bring to fulfilment the prayers which do not depart from the path of reason. Therefore, beloved son in the Lord, with grateful assent to your just requests, we confirm to you by apostolic authority the church of St James, situated in the city of Florence, which Julius, bishop of that city of happy memory, with the consent of the chapter of Florence, granted to your church; together with its burial ground and parish, and with the definite boundaries expressly set down in the charter which that bishop delivered to you and to the church of St Salvius concerning that grant. We confirm it as you rightfully and without dispute possess it, and strengthen it by the protection of this writing. We decree that no person whatsoever [Col. 1477B] may be permitted to infringe this page of our confirmation or in any way, with rash presumption, oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, the fourth day before the Nones of May [4 May].

XCII. He appoints Hugh, dean of Paris, and the abbot of St Germain-des-Prés as judges between the canons of Beauvais and the monks of St Lucian. (Verona, 21 May.)

[LOUVET, *History of Beauvais*, 503.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons Hugh, dean of Paris, and the abbot of St Germain-des-Prés: greeting and apostolic blessing.

You should know that it has come to our hearing on behalf of our beloved sons the canons of Beauvais that, although of their own free will and devotion they have customarily been buried at the monastery of St Lucian of Beauvais, the monks of that church now strive to turn into a necessity what has hitherto been voluntary, and do not permit the aforesaid canons to choose burial elsewhere. Yet this is permitted to all Christ’s faithful by canonical institution. Since the truth of the foregoing could not be established, we have judged that its investigation should be entrusted to your discretion and diligence. We command your discretion, [Col. 1477D] once the parties have been summoned into your presence, to grant the said canons, with any appeal set aside, free authority by apostolic power to choose burial wherever they wish, unless the said monks show and prove some reasonable ground on which they may legally claim the burial of those canons as their own.

Given at Verona, the twelfth day before the Kalends of June [21 May].

XCIII. He confirms for the canons of St Ursus a vineyard given by the bishop of Aosta. (Verona, 30 May.)

[*Monumenta Historiae Patriae*, Charters, I, 941.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1478A] sons, the prior and brothers of St Ursus: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily grant assent to the just desires of petitioners, and bring to fulfilment the prayers which do not depart from the path of reason. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, with grateful assent to your just requests, we confirm to you, and through you to your church, by apostolic authority, the vineyard which our venerable brother, the bishop of Aosta, with the assent of his metropolitan and on the counsel of his canons, gave in pious consideration to your hospital for the building of a house for the poor. We confirm it as you possess it rightfully and without dispute, and strengthen it by the protection of this writing. Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted [Col. 1478B] to infringe this page of our confirmation or, with rash presumption, oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, the third day before the Kalends of June [30 May].

XCIV. He confirms the judgment delivered by arbiters between the monks of St Savinus and the canons of the cathedral church of Piacenza. (Verona, 30 May.)

[CAMPI, *History of Piacenza*, II, 368.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot and brothers of St Savinus: greeting and apostolic [Col. 1478C] blessing.

Whereas a dispute had arisen between you and our beloved sons, the canons of the cathedral church of Piacenza, concerning the offerings on the feast of St Savinus, the candles placed upon the altar, the tithes of five *braidae* [landed estates], other lands, and the boundaries of the wood of Clavena: both parties submitted to arbitrators. After hearing the arguments between you, they adjudged that the offerings coming into the hands of the priest who sings the Mass should belong to the canons; but that the candles should be placed on the altar for the celebration of Mass and should remain in the monastery.

Concerning the tithes, they ruled that the cathedral church should have the tithe from the *braida* of Mosiis; while the monastery should have the tithe from the *braida* of the bishop’s Turre, from the *braida* of Turricella, from the *braida* of Regello, from the *braida* belonging to the house of the sick, and from all the other lands of the monastery lying within the tithe-district of the cathedral church around the city—whether the monastery cultivates them itself or others cultivate them—the cathedral church shall have the tithe. Concerning the wood of Clavena, they ruled that the division and boundaries established upon oath by Erminulf Pollonus, Fulco Pollonus, and Oddo Pollonus should stand.

We decree that this arbitration, as it was accepted by both parties, is valid, and we confirm it by apostolic authority. Therefore let no one, etc.

Given at Verona, the third day before the Kalends of June [30 May].

XCV. To the abbot and convent of Fécamp.—That sons are not to be appointed in their fathers’ churches, but are instead to be removed. (Verona, 1 June.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXII, 502.]

[Col. 1479A]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot and convent of Fécamp: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since it is contrary to the sacred canons for a son to succeed his father directly in churches of God, and since God’s sanctuary cannot lawfully be possessed as though by hereditary right, we regard it as astonishing and improper that, in certain churches subject to your monastery in both jurisdictions, some persons, as we have learned, have succeeded their parents [Col. 1479B] and hold those churches contrary to canonical discipline, to the scandal of many. Therefore, by the authority of these present letters, we grant you free power under apostolic authority to remove from those churches persons who hold the said churches in this way. Yet those churches are to be canonically provided without appropriate delay with suitable persons, unless perhaps such holders have been there for so long, and have conducted themselves in such a manner, that they seem deservedly to be retained. Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted, etc.

Given at Verona, on the Kalends of June [1 June].

XCVI. He confirms for the canons of St Opportuna at Paris the church of the Holy Innocents. (Verona, 3 June.)

[FÉLIBIEN, *History of Paris*, III, 35.]

[Col. 1479C]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons the canons of St Opportuna: greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting that we readily grant assent to the just desires of petitioners, and bring to fulfilment the prayers which do not depart from the path of reason. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, with grateful assent to your just requests, we confirm to you, in the name of your church, by apostolic authority, the church of the Holy Innocents, as you rightfully and without dispute possess it and as is contained in the confirmation of Pope Alexander, our predecessor of happy memory; and we strengthen it by the protection of this writing. [Col. 1479D] Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe this page of our confirmation or, with rash presumption, oppose it. But if anyone should presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, the third day before the Nones of June [3 June].

XCVII. To the abbot and convent of Fécamp.—That no one may pronounce a sentence of excommunication or interdict against the church or its persons. (Verona, 4 June.)

[*Neustria pia*, 242.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved [Col. 1480A] sons Henry, abbot, and the convent of the monastery of Fécamp: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since it has been granted to you by the Apostolic See that no one may pronounce a sentence of excommunication or interdict against your church or persons, and since our venerable brother the archbishop of Rouen recently subjected one of your monks to excommunication and afterward absolved him at his own will, you fear that prejudice may thereby arise for your church. Wishing therefore to provide for your tranquillity, we decree by apostolic authority that no prejudice may arise from this for you or for the liberty of your church. Therefore let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe this page of our constitution, etc.

[Col. 1480B] Given at Verona, the second day before the Nones of June [4 June].

XCVIII. He exhorts all faithful people established throughout the province of Ravenna, and all who cross the bridge of St Mary of the Reno, to contribute toward completing the bridge. (Verona, 13 June.)

[TROMBELLI, *Memorie di Reno*, 435.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to all Christ’s faithful established throughout the province of Ravenna and to all crossing the bridge of St Mary of the Reno at Bologna: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Whenever by apostolic letters we invite your piety to perform works of mercy, you ought to do so all the more eagerly because, through the bestowal of alms, [Col. 1480C] forgiveness of sins is believed to be obtained more swiftly, as Holy Scripture declares: “As water extinguishes fire, so almsgiving extinguishes sin.” Since, therefore, much has been spent in past time on the aforesaid bridge of Saint Mary of Reno, in the district of Bologna, and it has not yet been brought to its due completion, we beseech you all in the Lord that, when its messengers come to you seeking alms, you may receive them kindly and extend to them the hand of mercy; so that through these and other good works which, by the Lord’s inspiration, you shall perform, you may be cleansed from the stains of your sins and may at last be joined to the number of those of whom the Gospel says: “Blessed are the merciful, [Col. 1480D] for they shall obtain mercy.”

Given at Verona, on the Ides of June.

XCIX. Privilege for the monastery of Saint Paul of Parma. (Verona, June 26.)

[AFFO, *History of Parma*, II, p. 394.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, ROMANA, abbess, and the sisters of the monastery of Saint Paul of Parma, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We desire that those measures which are established by our brethren and fellow bishops through prudent deliberation for the increase of religious worship should remain in their force and be strengthened by the authority of apostolic favor. We have learned, moreover, [Col. 1481A] from the rescript of our venerable brother G., bishop of Mantua, that the church of Saint Mary of Castello Godo, formerly established under the regular observances of religious women, but now—sins demanding it—fallen into decay both through the dissolution of its order and through improvident administration of temporal affairs, he has, with all its appurtenances, subjected by pious deliberation to your monastery for the reform of the order, and has confirmed this by the guarantee of his writing. Since the text of this rescript, offered to us by that bishop and recited in our presence, might perhaps be obliterated by oblivion hereafter, we have thought fit to append it to this present document:

“In the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, in the year from His birth 1185, in the third indiction, on Friday, [Col. 1481B] the fourth day after the beginning of January: Garsendonius, bishop of Mantua—not through supporting merits, but through divine grace bestowed—to Romana, venerable abbess of Saint Paul of Parma, and to her sisters, present and future, who devoutly serve and shall serve God there under the Rule of blessed Benedict, in perpetuity.

“Considering more attentively, and perceiving with clear truth, how greatly you possess, through the Lord’s beneficence, vigor in religion, ardor in charity, liberality in hospitality, and observance of upright conduct and divine praise, we continually and providently praise the Creator of all things, holding a firm hope and confidence that those persons who shall succeed us will obtain the same grace from the Lord’s bounty.

“Therefore, dearest sisters in Christ, we give, grant, and by this present document confirm to you, the aforesaid Romana, the church [Col. 1481C] of Saint Mary of Old Castello at Godo, which is known to have been established in the order of religious women by our venerable predecessor Hugh of holy memory, but which now, sins demanding it, has greatly fallen away from that order, together with all that it presently possesses and all that belongs to it or may hereafter be acquired by lawful means. And through you we grant it to the aforesaid monastery of Saint Paul, to preserve the same order in that place, with all obedience and honor due to us and our successors reserved, and with the agreements between the archpriest of Saint Martin and the same church of Saint Mary remaining ratified and firm, [Col. 1481D] as is set forth in the grant of our predecessor Lord Hugh; so that neither we nor our successors may at any time, for any reason, act contrary to this charter of donation.

“We have also thought it necessary to append this: the noble knights of Godo came to us repeatedly, urgently and humbly requesting that religion there might through us be reformed for the better. We received their prayers with so much the readier a mind because we knew them to proceed from the fountain of charity.

“Furthermore, lest any occasion for malicious dispute should arise between Archpriest Ambrose, who now is or shall for the time being be at the church of Saint Martin, and the present or future abbess of the monastery of Saint Paul, we strengthen and confirm by this present writing the agreements between him and the church of Saint [Col. 1482A] Mary: namely, that the women who now are, or in time to come shall be, in the church of Saint Mary shall receive a priest from the archpriest, if there is a suitable one in the aforesaid church. But if there is no such priest in the said church, or if a suitable cleric to be advanced to that office cannot be found with the consent of both parties, the women residing there at the time shall provide themselves with a Catholic priest and shall have him with the consent of the Catholic archpriest or bishop.

“The priest serving in the aforesaid church shall have no authority in the court of Godo to impose penance, visit the sick, bury the dead, or baptize anyone, except all those who dwell in and are devoted to the aforesaid [Col. 1482B] church, without the consent of the archpriest of the greater church. But if any of those who live in the court of Godo comes to death and wishes to bequeath something of his own to the aforesaid church and to have his body buried at that church, then, provided this pleases the sick person after the judgment of the greater church has first been obtained, he shall be carried by the clerics and priests of the greater church to the aforesaid church; and whatever is offered at the celebration of the Masses, whether to the priest of that church or to the greater church, shall be divided equally. One half shall be left to the sisters dwelling there.

“Moreover, at the four principal feasts of the year—namely, the Nativity and Resurrection of the Lord, Saint Mary, and Saint Lawrence—whatever is offered at the celebration of the Masses, whether to the priest of that church or of the greater [Col. 1482C] church, shall be divided equally, and one half shall be left to the aforesaid church. But if the aforesaid priest commits an offense in criminal matters, in the presence of the community of religious women and the clerics dwelling there, he shall be corrected reasonably and according to rule by the archpriest. In chapter, in the litanies, and at baptism with the brethren of the greater church [lacuna]. Because it appeared to all that the matters stated above were sufficient [lacuna] or may at any time be offered, free from all dues and [lacuna] released from payment both in offerings and in other matters, with the consent of Archpriest Ambrose and the brethren of the greater church, namely [lacuna] atii and the duke.

“[Col. 1482D] We establish and immutably confirm these things, and have ordered this memorial writing to be made thereof. And so that this ordinance may remain firm and inviolate forever, and that the aforesaid church or those dwelling there may suffer no further molestation or exaction from our successors, whether bishops or archpriests and clerics of that greater church, we impose and immutably confirm a penalty of ten Milanese pounds—this writing nevertheless remaining forever in its full force and validity. And that it may be more truly believed and more firmly accepted by all, we have ordered it to be marked with our seal and have confirmed it by the subscription of our own hand.”

[Col. 1483A] We therefore receive that same church of Saint Paul, with all its appurtenances, under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves; and, desiring that the grant itself should stand as valid, as it was made by the same bishop with reasonable foresight and is contained in his aforesaid authentic instrument, we confirm by apostolic authority to you and to your church the same church with all its appurtenances, as you possess it lawfully and without dispute, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. Let no person whatsoever, therefore, be permitted rashly to disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, infringe this charter of our protection and confirmation, or in any way oppose it. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person shall knowingly attempt in future rashly to act against this charter of our protection and confirmation, then, after a second or third warning, [Col. 1483B] unless he makes fitting satisfaction for his offense, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and office; let him know himself liable before the divine judgment for the iniquity he has committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of the aforesaid monastery may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

Given at Verona, on the sixth day before the Kalends of July [26 June].

C. It confirms to the monastery of Cluny the monastery of Saint Germanus of Auxerre. (Verona, June 27.)

[*Bullarium Cluniacense*, p. 85.]

[Col. 1483C]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HUGH, abbot, and the convent of Cluny, greeting and apostolic blessing.

The more especially your monastery belongs by right to blessed Peter, is subject directly to our care and protection without any intermediary, and you and your predecessors therein, subject to the discipline of the heavenly Master, have hitherto spread more widely, through the infusion of the Holy Spirit, the fragrance of upright conduct and of the religious observance maintained in your order, the more readily are we bound to preserve your rights unimpaired and to admit more favorably the just petitions of your devotion. [Col. 1483D] For, as has become known to us from the rescripts of S., formerly count of Blois, and A., his wife; of Urban II and Paschal, Roman pontiffs of blessed memory; and from the seals of our beloved sons B., cardinal deacon of Saint Angelo, and S., cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, legates of the Apostolic See, which were transmitted to our presence: the monastery of Saint Germanus of Auxerre, in which, through the negligence of its administrators, the discipline of regular observance had so utterly perished and its temporal resources had so failed that its custody was entrusted to degraded persons, was granted by our predecessor Urban II, at the request of the aforesaid count, patron of that monastery, of Hubald, bishop of Auxerre of good memory, and of many others, to blessed Hugh, then abbot [Col. 1484A] of your monastery, and to his successors, to be reformed according to the Rule of blessed Benedict and possessed perpetually in future under the governance of the monastery of Cluny. Yet the monastery itself was not to lack the care of an abbot. This grant and the donation of the aforesaid count were subsequently confirmed by our predecessor Paschal.

Following in the footsteps of our predecessors, after their example we decree that the same grant is valid and confirm it by this present writing, establishing that no person whatsoever may be permitted to infringe this charter of our confirmation or rashly oppose it. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty [Col. 1484B] God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, on the seventh day before the Kalends of July [25 June].

CI. It confirms to the abbot of Vézelay and his successors the use of the mitre, gloves, and ring. (Verona, July 5.)

[LAUNOII, *Works*, II, I, 288.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot and convent of Saint Mary Magdalene of Vézelay, greeting and apostolic blessing.

As a mark of ecclesiastical dignity, insignia of offices have been devised, which the most holy Roman Church distributes with fitting liberality to individuals, and permits devout sons, as she judges fitting, [Col. 1484C] both to receive and to possess. Therefore, moved by reverence for blessed Mary Magdalene, whose sacred body rests in your church, and by the merit of your devotion, we grant and by apostolic authority confirm the use of the mitre, gloves, and ring to you, son abbot, and to your successors.

Let no one, therefore, etc.

Given at Verona, on the third day before the Nones of July [5 July].

CII. He commands U[bert], bishop of Acqui, not to permit the rights of the canons to be violated by the monks of Saint Peter. (Verona, July 6.)

[MORIONDI, *Monuments of Acqui*, I, 86.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother F. U., bishop of Acqui, greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1484D] Upon the complaint of our beloved sons, your canons, concerning our beloved sons the abbot and monks of Saint Peter of Acqui, we recall that we commanded them not in any way to encroach upon the bounds of the parish of the city and suburb of Acqui, which are known to have been adjudged to the Church of Acqui by the judgment of Algisius, formerly archbishop of Milan of good memory; nor to admit anyone from that parish to public penances, funeral rites, or other parochial ministrations; nor in any other manner to inflict upon them injury or burden concerning that parish. Since, therefore, as we have learned from their repeated complaint, they have not ceased hitherto, in contempt of the apostolic command, [Col. 1485A] from disturbing their rights, by the authority of this present letter we command your brotherhood, with all appeal set aside, to compel the aforesaid abbot and monks of Saint Peter to observe the sentence already mentioned according to the tenor of the apostolic command, and to desist from troubling their brethren concerning that parish.

Given at Verona, on the second day before the Nones of July [6 July].

CIII. He confirms the ordinance of the canons of the Church of Piacenza: “that, so long as the canons remain honorably in the schools and diligently in study, they are to have for their maintenance one third of all revenues which they would receive were they present in that church; one third being left to the brethren, the other portion is to be assigned to common use.” (Verona, July 7.)

[CAMPI, *History of Piacenza*, II, 369.]

[Col. 1485B]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the chapter of Piacenza, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Those things which are reasonably established by ministers of the Church ought to remain firm and unimpaired, and, lest they may be rashly altered by anyone, should be strengthened by apostolic protection. Since, moreover, with consideration for the common good, you have established by prudent deliberation that, so long as the canons of your church remain honorably in the schools and diligently in study, they are to have for their support one third of all revenues which they would receive if present in that church, while one third is left to the brethren and the other portion [Col. 1485C] is assigned to common use: we confirm that ordinance by apostolic authority, as prudently made and received, and strengthen it by the protection of this present writing.

Let no one, therefore, etc.

Given at Verona, on the Nones of July [7 July].

CIV. He forbids the archpriest and canons of Bologna to inflict injuries upon the brethren of Saint Mary of Reno. (Verona, July 15.)

[TROMBELLI, *Memoirs of Reno*, 380.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the [lacuna] archpriest and canons of Bologna, [Col. 1485D] greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since, on account of their religious life and devotion, we love our beloved sons Hugh, prior, and the brethren of Saint Mary of Reno with special affection beyond the common obligation, we neither will nor ought to suffer them to be unlawfully troubled by you, who ought to assist them in their rights. Therefore, by apostolic authority we forbid you to presume in any way to harass them concerning tithes or other matters granted by the bishops of Bologna and archbishops of Ravenna, and subsequently confirmed by our predecessors and by ourselves; for this would be exceedingly grave and vexatious to us, and we could not leave it uncorrected any longer.

Given at Verona, on the Ides of July.

CV. He grants to G., dean, and the chapter of Chartres “that, if anyone has carried off property of their church and his offense is manifest, the robber may not evade ecclesiastical discipline by the refuge of an appeal.” (Verona, July 15.)

[*The Penitential of Theodore*, II, 563.]

[Col. 1486A]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons G., dean, and the chapter of Chartres, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since the remedy of appeal was devised for the assistance of the oppressed, not for the defense of evildoers, we wish and ought to provide that wrongdoers may not with impunity lay violent hands upon ecclesiastical goods under the pretext of an appeal. [Col. 1486B] Moved by this consideration, we establish by apostolic authority that, if anyone has carried off property of your church and his offense is manifest, or if before the bishop or archdeacon in whose archdeaconry the wrongdoer resides you have canonically proved your allegation, the robber may not evade ecclesiastical discipline by the refuge of an appeal. Let no person whatsoever, therefore, be permitted to infringe this charter of our ordinance or rashly oppose it; but should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, on the Ides of July.

CVI. He confirms certain possessions to Hugh, abbot, and the canons of the Church of Prémontré. (Verona, July 21.)

[LE PAIGE, *Bibliotheca Praemonstratensis*, 640.]

[Col. 1486C]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HUGH, abbot of Prémontré, and the other abbots and canons of the Premonstratensian Order, present and future, professing the regular life, in perpetuity.

Although unworthy, we have been placed by the Lord’s ordinance in the exalted watchtower of the Apostolic See; we are consequently constrained to be concerned for the condition of every individual, and are bound sincerely to embrace those things which pertain to the increase of religion and the adornment of virtue, so that the peace of religious persons may be secure from every disturbance [Col. 1486D] and preserved unimpaired from the yoke of worldly oppression when fortified by apostolic protection.

Considering, therefore, how your religion and order, resplendent with much glory of merits and fragrant with the grace of holiness, has stretched forth its branches from sea to sea, we have thought fit to cherish that order itself and all houses of the same order under the protection of apostolic guardianship and to strengthen them by this present privilege. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, graciously assenting to your just petitions, after the example of Alexander and Lucius, Roman pontiffs of happy memory, our predecessors, we strengthen by apostolic authority and fortify by the privilege of this present writing all regular institutions and arrangements which you have made by common consent, or by that of the greater and sounder part, as they are set forth below. [Col. 1487A] Namely: that the canonical order, as it is known to have been established in the Church of Prémontré according to the Rule of blessed Augustine and the ordinances of Norbert of revered memory, formerly founder of the Premonstratensian Order, and of his successors, in a white habit, shall be observed inviolate forever in all churches of the same order. Likewise, the same books pertaining to the divine office shall be uniformly kept by all churches of the same order; and the remaining provisions, as they stand in the privilege or diploma of Lucius III for those same persons, down to what follows.

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 1487B] I, Henry, bishop of Albano. I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, of the title of Calixtus. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Ralph, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the day before the Kalends of July [30 June], in the fifth indiction, in the year 1187 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the second year of the pontificate of our lord Pope Urban [Col. 1487C] III.

CVII. He confirms certain possessions given by Count Robert to the house of Saint Thomas at Paris. (Verona, July 22.)

[DUBOIS, *Ecclesiastical History of Paris*, II, 182.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son WILLIAM, priest and administrator of the house of Saint Thomas the Martyr at Paris, greeting and apostolic blessing.

When princes of the world, divinely inspired, assign some of their goods to pious uses, we ought to support them in their good purpose; and, lest their act be altered through anyone’s malice, to grant them apostolic protection. As was represented in our hearing, [Col. 1487D] our chosen son, the noble Count Robert, out of love for divine mercy, assigned certain houses which he possessed at Paris, with certain revenues, to the provision of poor clerics, with the consent of his wife and children; religious persons having been established by God’s authority in that place, who ought likewise to devote themselves with them to the same praiseworthy work. Since, therefore, our gracious son in Christ Philip, illustrious king of the Franks, and his queen, his wife, have asked us—and the aforesaid count has also asked—that we should strengthen his donation by our authority, we confirm it by apostolic authority, as piously and laudably made, and fortify it by the protection of this present writing. We further establish that the diocesan bishop shall bless a cemetery for the use [Col. 1488A] of the brethren and their household, and of the sick who die there.

Moreover, let no one presume to extort tithes from you on your newly cultivated lands, which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or on the produce from the food of your animals, your gardens, or your houses. Let no person be permitted to infringe this charter of our confirmation and prohibition or rashly oppose it. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of August [22 July].

CVIII. To Walter, archbishop of Rouen—That nothing is to be altered after an appeal. (Verona, July 31.)

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXII, 301.]

[Col. 1488B]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother WALTER, archbishop of Rouen, greeting and apostolic blessing.

We are bound to give more ready assistance to those who raise the voice of appeal for their protection, and, while an appeal is pending, to employ pastoral care lest they be burdened by the malice of anyone. For since the remedy of appeal was devised to assist the oppressed, it is incumbent upon you, insofar as the order of law requires, to safeguard their security. Therefore, since in your province, as we have heard, [Col. 1488C] it often happens that both ecclesiastical and secular persons, after an appeal, are despoiled of possessions or other goods, we grant you by this present letter free authority, if you ascertain that anything affecting the condition of persons in your province has been altered to their prejudice after an impediment of appeal has been raised, to restore it—with the appeal set aside—to the state in which it stood at the time of the appeal, lest appellants suffer loss of their rights. Establishing that no person whatsoever may be permitted to infringe this charter of our concession or rashly oppose it. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul [Col. 1488D].

Given at Verona, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of August [22 July].

CIX. He commands all abbots of the Premonstratensian Order established in Germany and Saxony to attend the general chapter at Prémontré every year. (Verona, August 1.)

[HUGO, *Premonstratensian Annals*, II, 128.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, all abbots of the Premonstratensian Order established in Germany and Saxony, greeting and apostolic blessing.

From a report transmitted to us by the Premonstratensian Order, we have learned that from the very origin [Col. 1489A] of your order it has been established, and by the privileges of Roman pontiffs confirmed by the authority of the Apostolic See, that the abbots of that order shall gather once a year at Prémontré for a general chapter, in which, after jointly discussing the observances of the order, they shall correct what needs correction and make arrangements for what must be ordered. But because many of you, in the time when the storm of the past schism spread more widely through those regions, withdrew yourselves from the general chapter, you have since then, as we have heard, almost adopted as a custom that you come to the aforesaid chapter either never or very rarely. We regard this as all the more grave and unworthy because, through greater lukewarmness, whatever was established for the preservation of discipline [Col. 1489B] is seen to perish through your negligence.

Therefore, that you may prove yourselves sons not of withdrawal but of obedience, by apostolic letters we command and expressly order you all, with every appeal and objection set aside, to cleanse away the foulness of past negligence by the hand of ready diligence, so that the brightness of renewed fervor may shine forth and dispel whatever clouds of former lukewarmness darken the aforesaid order.

Accordingly, we wish you to take heed and command you to observe that, notwithstanding any rescript obtained by suppressing the truth, you shall come every year to the general chapter at the Church of Prémontré, as [Col. 1489C] has been established and observed from ancient times, for the correction of that order; unless perhaps you are detained by such impediments as may, according to your paternal traditions, regularly excuse you. Otherwise, we will and command that the sentence which the aforesaid general chapter pronounces against absentees shall be deemed valid and observed inviolate.

Given at Verona, on the Kalends of August [1 August].

CX. To the archbishop of Tours—At the request of Philip, king of the Franks, he grants him a truce in order that he may reach an amicable settlement with the Church of Dol. (Verona, September 4.)

[MARTEN., *Treasury*, III, 911.]

[Col. 1489D]

Although the affair pending between you and the Church of Dol has been prolonged too long through the truces granted you by the Apostolic See, so that proceedings for its decision ought now rightly to be undertaken—especially because certain witnesses for the Church of Dol were received and examined by Pope Alexander of revered memory while he was staying at Tusculum; and thereafter, according to the tenor of that pope’s letters, by command of Pope Lucius, our predecessor of pious memory, witnesses were produced by both parties before our beloved sons the dean of Le Mans, J. of Vieuxpont, archdeacon of Rouen, and Master Hugh of Genoa, provost of Saint Mary of the Castle, [Col. 1490A] and their depositions were written down and presented to apostolic inspection—yet, awaiting the long-standing controversy between you and the aforesaid Church to be ended by an agreed settlement with the consent of the parties, at the request of our dearest son Philip, illustrious king of the Franks, for whom we both wish and ought to do whatever we can with God, we have thought fit to extend to you and to the aforesaid church committed to you a truce from the coming month of March for one year, peren- [lacuna].

[Col. 1490B] Thus, if within the prescribed term that controversy has not been ended by agreement, you shall appear before apostolic inspection, either in person or through suitable and sufficiently instructed representatives, to answer the aforesaid Church of Dol and to receive judgment according to God and truth. This shall be notwithstanding the letters which your messengers prematurely obtained without the knowledge of the aforesaid elect and the canons of the said Church of Dol, the tenor of which we have ordered to be altered in our presence, according to the present form, while those messengers were still before us.

Your brotherhood shall diligently take care not to show yourself obstinate and unyielding in making a settlement on the occasion of this truce; for if this is established to be the truth of the matter, we shall revoke the same truce and, with God’s help, proceed to what is just.

Given at Verona, on the Kalends of September [1 September].

CXI. Privilege for the nunnery of Saint Peter of Cremella. (Verona, September 12.)

[FRIZI, *Memoirs of Monza*, II, 73.]

[Col. 1490C]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, the abbess and sisters of the monastery of Saint Peter of Cremella, greeting and apostolic blessing.

An authentic instrument of Robald, formerly archbishop of Milan of pious memory, having been presented to us concerning the dispute that had arisen between your monastery and the church of Saint John of Monza over seven articles explicitly set forth in that instrument, we plainly observe [Col. 1490D] that the questions proposed were settled by a definitive judgment. Therefore, we confirm by apostolic authority that judgment, as it was canonically rendered by the same archbishop and is contained in the authentic writing mentioned above, and fortify it by the protection of this present document. Let no person whatsoever be permitted to infringe this charter of our confirmation or rashly oppose it. Should anyone presume to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

Given at Verona, on the second day before the Ides of September [12 September].

CXII. He grants to the abbot and convent of Saint Denis “that no archbishop or bishop may dare to pronounce a sentence of excommunication or interdict against them, or against any one of their monks, whether in head or members, without the authority of the Roman pontiff, or of a legate sent from his side, or possessing a special mandate in this matter, or even without the command of their abbot.” (Verona, September 12.)

[DOUBLET, *History of Saint-Denis*, 523.]

[Col. 1491A]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot and convent of the monastery of Saint Denis, greeting and apostolic blessing.

It is fitting and consonant with reason that we should show marks of greater favor to those who belong especially to blessed Peter and to ourselves by right, and should take care to assist them more mercifully against the burdens imposed by those who harass them. [Col. 1491B] Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, favorably assenting to your just petitions, we have thought fit by this present document to prohibit any archbishop or bishop from daring to pronounce a sentence of excommunication or interdict against you, or against any one of your monks, whether in head or members, without the authority of the Roman pontiff, or of a legate sent from his side, or possessing a special mandate in this matter, or even without the command of their abbot. Let no person whatsoever, therefore, etc.

Given at Verona, on the second day before the Ides of September [12 September].

CXIII. He confirms the parochial boundaries of the churches of Saint Paul and Saint Vitalis at Verona, established by two cardinals. (Verona, September 22.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia Sacra*, V, 806.]

[Col. 1491C]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ADRIAN, archpriest, and the canons of Verona, greeting and apostolic blessing.

Those things which are established for the peace and tranquility of churches through the providence of the Apostolic See ought to remain firm and unimpaired; and, lest they be corrupted by anyone’s malice, they should be committed to the record of letters and strengthened by the text of our document. Accordingly, since after many disputes which it long happened were conducted between you and our beloved sons, the brethren of the Order of the Temple, concerning the parochial boundaries of the two churches of Saint Paul and Saint Vitalis, it pleased each party to choose our determination: [Col. 1491D] having sent our beloved sons Soff., cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Via Lata, and R., cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, as examiners for the investigation of this matter, we deem valid their designation of the parishes of each church and command that it be observed without challenge. Namely: all that lies from the house of Alioci of Monte Cleda, including that house, in a straight line to the house of Tridentin, including that house, in a straight line to the house of Lanfranchi Muxolin., and including that house, toward the church of Saint Paul, shall belong to the parish of Saint Paul; and all that lies from those houses and boundaries toward the church of Saint Vitalis shall freely and without any contradiction [Col. 1492A] be reckoned to the parish of Saint Vitalis. And so that this definition may remain inviolate for all time, we confirm it by apostolic authority, as reasonably made, and fortify it by the protection of this present writing. Let no one, therefore, etc.

Given at Verona, on the tenth day before the Kalends of October [22 September].

IN THE YEAR 1187. CXIV. He permits Sueno, bishop of Aarhus, after resigning his bishopric, to enter a monastery.

[LANGEBECK, *Diplomata Suenonis*, V, p. 255.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to the venerable brother SUENO, bishop of Aarhus, greeting and apostolic blessing.

When matters are requested of us that appear to proceed from concern for salvation, we ought not to show ourselves reluctant, but rather readily grant our consent to petitioners. Now, as has been represented to us on your behalf, considering the difficulty of episcopal administration, which is often entangled in many occupations, you have resolved to withdraw to the peace of the cloister; and concerning this you judged apostolic authority must be sought, without which you would not be permitted to do so. Therefore, wishing in this matter to comply with your requests, by the tenor of this present document we grant you leave, whenever you wish, freely to resign that bishopric and transfer yourself to a place of repose.  
[Note: [Col. 1491] This diploma cannot have been issued later than 1187; for Pope Urban died in that year.]

## CXV. Confirms the goods and rights of the monastery of St Nicholas on the Venetian shore. (Verona, January 6.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, V, 1247.]

[Col. 1492C]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons MATTHEW, abbot of the monastery of St Nicholas, situated on the shore of the port of Rialto, and to his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

A pious request ought to be fulfilled by a corresponding effect, so that sincerity of devotion may be made commendably manifest and the benefit requested may undoubtedly acquire force. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and, following the example of our predecessors of blessed memory, the Roman pontiffs Callistus, Alexander, and Lucius, we receive under the devotion of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present document, the aforesaid monastery of St Nicholas. Dominic Contarini, doge of Venice of good memory, together with Dominic, patriarch of Grado, Dominic, bishop of Olivolo, and the whole Venetian clergy and people, granted that it should be built upon an estate belonging to him in his own right on the shore of the port of Rialto, and decreed that brethren of the monastic order should thereafter dwell in that place.

We decree that the possessions, goods, and rights which have been bestowed upon that place by the same doge or by other faithful persons—in the empire of Constantinople, Corinth, Dyrrachium, Rhodes, Almyros, Jerusalem, Acre, the Italian kingdom, [Col. 1493A] Bologna, Padua, Istria, the March, and within the province of Venice, or in any places whatsoever—and whatever else the aforesaid monastery may, by the generosity of kings or princes or by the offerings of the faithful, lawfully acquire in possessions or otherwise, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any cunning of fraud or violence, except the man whom the brethren, by common consent, or the sounder part of the brethren, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of St Benedict, shall judge to be chosen.

We therefore decree that no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations whatsoever; but that all things be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those uses for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the due right of the bishop of Olivolo solely in the consecration of abbots and in the payment, each year at the feast of St Nicholas, of the dinner imposed upon your monastery. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, let him, after a second and third warning, unless he corrects his presumption by fitting satisfaction, be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know that he is guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve their rights to that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Peter de Bono, priest-cardinal of the title of St Susanna, have subscribed. I, Laborans, priest-cardinal of St Mary in Trastevere, have subscribed. I, Pandulf, priest-cardinal of the title of the Twelve Apostles, [Col. 1493D] have subscribed. I, Adelard, priest-cardinal of the title of St Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Hyacinth, deacon-cardinal of St Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed. I, Gratian, deacon-cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Bobo, deacon-cardinal of St Angelo, have subscribed. I, Godfrey, deacon-cardinal of St Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Roland, deacon-cardinal of St Mary in Portico, have subscribed. [Col. 1494A] I, Rudolph, deacon-cardinal of St George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Moses, canon of the Lateran, acting in place of the chancellor, on the eighth day before the Ides of January, in the fourth indiction, in the year 1186 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban III.

## CXVI. Confirms the privileges of the monastery of Morimond. (Verona, January 7.)

[UGHELLI, *Italia sacra*, IV, 169.  
Note: [Col. 1493] Here only the subscriptions are printed. Let the reader consult the privilege granted to the same monastery by Alexander III, which reproduces Urban’s bull word for word. It is found in volume CC of the *Patrologia*.]

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Henry, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Peter de Bono, priest-cardinal of the title of St Susanna, have subscribed. [Col. 1494B] I, Laborans, priest-cardinal of St Mary in Trastevere, of the title of St Callistus, have subscribed. I, Pandulf, priest-cardinal of the title of the Twelve Apostles, have subscribed. I, Melchior, priest-cardinal of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius, have subscribed. I, Hyacinth, deacon-cardinal of St Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed. I, Gratian, deacon-cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Bobo, deacon-cardinal of St Angelo, have subscribed. I, Soffredus, deacon-cardinal of St Mary in Via Lata, have subscribed. I, Roland, deacon-cardinal of St Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Radulph, deacon-cardinal of St George at the Golden Veil, [Col. 1494C] have subscribed.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal of the Holy Roman Church and chancellor, on the seventh day before the Ides of January, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1186 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban III.

## CXVII. Privilege for the monastery of Alta Valle. (Verona, January 12.)

[LUPI, *Codex diplomaticus Bergomensis*, II, 1355.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ISRAEL, abbot, and the brethren of the monastery of Alta Valle in the parish of Bergamo, present and future, to be regularly appointed: in perpetuity.

The authority of the Apostolic See entrusted to us [Col. 1494D] exhorts us to extend the protection of our guardianship to religious places and persons that devoutly request aid. For just as no effect ought to be granted to those who ask for unjust things, so the petition of those who seek what is lawful and just ought not to be delayed. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves the monastery of Alta Valle, in which you are dedicated to divine service, and fortify it by the privilege of this present document. First, indeed, we decree that the monastic order known to have been established there according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict [Col. 1495A] shall be preserved there inviolate for all time.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or by other just means, with the Lord’s help acquire, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among them we have determined to specify the following by name:

On the east, the land of Gaverino, Apelliano, Milonio, and Tercio; the mountain called Pelsinus; on the west, as the little valley called Vallis Jumella extends; from the mountains, the road of Altino; the estate called Pellianus, with its possessions; [Col. 1495B] the new estate, with its possessions; the chapel of Saint [lacuna] of Campania, with its possessions; the chapel of the Holy Saviour of Bergamo, with its possessions; the mountain called Armentaticus; the mountain called Cardenianus; the mountain called Mallia; likewise the donations made to you and your monastery by Gregory, Girard, and Vulla, bishops of Bergamo of good memory, with the counsel and assent of their chapter; and further those which our venerable brother John, bishop of Brescia, concerning the church of St George of Tegio, and Altemanius, bishop of Trent of good memory, concerning the church of St Lawrence of Trent, made to you with the assent of their canons and confirmed by perpetual documents. As those documents contain, and as you possess these things justly and peaceably, we confirm them to you and, through you, to the monastery by apostolic authority.

Upon the death of you, the present abbot of that place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be placed over it by any fraud or violence, except the person whom the brethren, by common consent [lacuna] of the sounder counsel, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of blessed Benedict, shall judge to be elected. Further, no one shall presume to demand or extort tithes from you of your newly cleared lands which you cultivate with your own hands or at your own expense, or from the nourishment of your animals.

We therefore decree that no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, [Col. 1495D] or harass it by any vexations whatsoever; but that all things be preserved whole for the benefit in every way of those uses for whose governance and support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, let him, after a second or third warning, unless he makes amends for his offence by suitable satisfaction, lose the dignity of his power and honour; let him know that he is guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and at the final judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve their rights to that [Col. 1496A] place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

In the circle: “To you, O Lord, I have lifted up my soul.”

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Henry, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, James, deacon-cardinal of St Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed. I, Gratian, deacon-cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Bobo, deacon-cardinal of St Angelo, have subscribed. I, Peter de Boi [lacuna], priest-cardinal of St Susanna, have subscribed. [Col. 1496B] I, Laborans, priest-cardinal of St Mary in Trastevere, of the title of Callistus, have subscribed. I, Pandulf, priest-cardinal of the title of the Twelve Apostles, have subscribed. I, Melchior, priest-cardinal of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius, have subscribed.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Roman Church, on the second day before the Ides of January, in the fourth indiction, in the year 1186 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban III.

## CXVIII. Confirms the possessions and privileges of the convent of St Zacharias at Venice. (Fragment.) (Verona, February 17.)

[CORNELII, *Ecclesiae Venetae*, XI, 377.]

[Col. 1496C]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, CASOTA, abbess of the monastery of St Zacharias of Venice, and her sisters, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity, etc.

[lacuna] They shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and for those who succeed you. Among them we have determined to specify the following by name: the place itself in which the aforesaid monastery is situated, with all its appurtenances; the manor situated in the place called Petriolo, with the church of St Thomas and all its appurtenances; the manor situated in the place called Cona, with the church of St Mary and all its appurtenances; the manor situated in the place [Col. 1496D] called Runco, with all its appurtenances and with the church of St Mary; the manor situated in the place called Clugia, with all its appurtenances; and all other things as are contained in the bull of Pope Alexander III of happy memory.

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church. L. S. I, Henry, bishop of Albano. I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina. I, Peter de Bono, priest-cardinal of the title of St Susanna. I, Laborans, priest-cardinal of St Mary in Trastevere, of the title of Callistus. I, Pandulf, priest-cardinal of the title of the Twelve Apostles. I, Melchior, priest-cardinal of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. And six others.

[Col. 1497A] Given at Verona, through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of March, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1186 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban III.

## CXIX. To Wichmann, archbishop of Magdeburg—concerning injuries inflicted upon the Roman Church by Emperor Frederick, and requesting that he intervene as mediator for peace. (Verona, February 24.)

[MANSI, *Concilia*, XXII, 506.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother, the archbishop of Magdeburg: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1497B] That love which, poured forth through the Spirit in the hearts of the elect (Romans 5), binds the body of the Church together in the structure of its strength—so that the head cleaves to the members in an ineffable union, while the serviceable diversity of the members does not depart from the unity of the head—has established firmly in our heart the purpose of holding you more sincerely within the bowels of Jesus Christ. Let your brotherhood therefore know that, burning with the ardour of this love toward you and the Church committed to you, we have spiritual confidence in you: just as we embrace your fatherhood with a certain bond of special affection, so we shall always be abundantly delighted in your good dispositions by the praiseworthy return received from your devotion.

Accordingly, prompted by this confidence, we set before you the cause of our excessive distress, [Col. 1497C] so that, sharing our troubles, we may receive greater consolation in the Lord from your prudence and support. The exalted imperial majesty has often been warned by us to restore to the Roman Church the possessions it holds under occupation; yet it has not replied with the serenity it ought, nor does it appear willing to accomplish that by which a firm peace and concord might arise between the Church and the Empire. Therefore we have thought fit to make this known to you by apostolic letters, earnestly asking and commanding that, when you come to those regions in which your brotherhood may obtain an audience with him, you do not omit to persuade and advise him to look with a more kindly [Col. 1497D] eye upon the Church of God, as befits his glory and salvation, and, as becomes his magnificent sovereignty, utterly cut away with praiseworthy mercy the matter and fuel of discord from the midst. But if, perhaps, despite your warning he does not do this, know that the blame for the dissension and hateful strife must be laid upon that side which appears responsible for the breach, since the power and facility of remedy remain in its hand.

Given at Verona, on the sixth day before the Kalends of March.

## CXX. Rebukes B[aldwin], archbishop of Canterbury, because he subjected the prior and brethren of the Church of Canterbury to various injuries and disregarded their appeal to the Apostolic See. He commands that “within ten days he shall publicly declare that sentences of suspension pronounced against the prior and the other brethren have no force, and that he shall restore to their former state whatever he attempted after the first appeal to the prejudice of their rights.” He refers to this in the following letter. (Verona, March 1.)

[TWISDEN, *Historiae Anglicanae Scriptores*, I, 1491.]

[Col. 1498A]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother B., archbishop of Canterbury, legate of the Apostolic See: greeting and apostolic blessing.

When we recall the fervour of your religious life and the office of governance which you have undertaken in the Church of God for the care of the salvation of the faithful, we cannot but grieve if anything concerning the acts of your brotherhood is laid before us that contradicts your dignity and episcopal office. For it is fitting and consonant with reason that, just as we love you as a special member of the Church with sincere love in the Lord, so we should have a special concern for your manner of life and conduct, because we would regard it as no small injury to you if the reputation of your praiseworthy religious life should, God forbid, be harmed upon any occasion.

Now our beloved son, the prior of your church, appearing before us with certain of his brethren, respectfully represented that since your promotion—by which they believed the condition of their convent would in every way be increased to the honour of God—they have suffered from you outrageous burdens and daily endure still graver ones. Since, on account of these matters, they appealed to the Apostolic See, appointing as the deadline the Sunday called “Laetare Jerusalem,” to pass over other matters for the moment, you, in what we regard as astonishing and unworthy, did not defer to that appeal, but in its execution suspended one of the brethren, who afterwards, as is said, was removed from that very church at your command. After the same appeal, although the prior and brethren placed themselves and their property under apostolic protection, you nevertheless suspended the prior, alleging against him that he had permitted one of his brethren to come into our presence and had received another who had appealed into the church and the fellowship of the brethren. After the said prior, because of the aforementioned burdens, had set out to come to the Apostolic See, you are said to have instituted certain secular canons in the basilica which you propose to build to their gravest harm, despite the brethren’s appeals and protests; to have assigned to them the churches belonging to the brethren; and to have suspended from service at the altar all who had appealed.

Although we await your representatives and envoys, within the period set for the appeal, concerning the principal questions, we nevertheless do not wish to leave uncorrected those acts said to have been done in contempt of the Apostolic See, however much we may wish to defer to your brotherhood. By apostolic authority we therefore command and direct you publicly to declare, within ten days [Col. 1499A] after receipt of this letter, that the sentences of suspension pronounced, after the appeal to us had been lodged, against the aforesaid prior and the other brethren of the same church have no force; and you are not to omit restoring to its former state whatever you attempted after the first appeal to the prejudice of their rights. Know that, if within the prescribed period you delay to perform what we command, we shall by no means be able to endure further injuries to the Church in this matter. We have already commanded our beloved sons, the abbots of Battle, Faversham, and St Augustine’s, to carry this out by apostolic authority, the appeal being set aside; notwithstanding any letters obtained from the Apostolic See that prejudice truth and justice.

Given at Verona, on the Kalends of March.

## CXXI. Informs the abbots of Battle, Faversham, and St Augustine’s what he commanded the archbishop of Canterbury in the preceding letter. He directs as follows: “If the aforesaid archbishop delays to carry out what we command within the prescribed period, you shall put it into execution.” (Verona, March 1.)

[Ibid., 1492.]

[Col. 1499B]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbots of Battle, Faversham, and St Augustine’s: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our beloved son, the prior of the Church of Canterbury, coming to the Apostolic See with certain of his brethren, carefully represented to us that they have suffered outrageous burdens from our venerable brother B., archbishop of Canterbury and legate of the Apostolic See, since his promotion, [Col. 1499C] and daily endure still graver ones. Since, because of these matters, they appealed to the Apostolic See, appointing as the deadline the Sunday called “Laetare Jerusalem,” that same archbishop, not deferring to the appeal, suspended one of the brethren in its execution; and he too was afterwards, as is said, removed from that very church at the archbishop’s command. After the same appeal, although the prior and brethren placed themselves and their property under apostolic protection, he nevertheless suspended the prior, alleging against him that he had permitted one of his brethren to come into our presence and had received another who had appealed into the church and the fellowship of the brethren. After the said prior had set out for the Apostolic See because of the aforementioned burdens, the aforesaid archbishop is said to have instituted certain secular canons in the basilica which, to the brethren’s gravest harm, he is said to have built, despite their appeals and protests; to have assigned the brethren’s churches to them; and to have suspended all who had appealed from service at the altar.

Although we await the archbishop’s representatives and envoys concerning the principal questions, within the period set for the appeal, we do not wish to leave uncorrected those things so manifestly done in contempt of the Apostolic See. We therefore commanded the same archbishop by apostolic authority that, within ten days after receipt of our letters, he should publicly declare that the sentences of suspension pronounced, after the appeal to us had been lodged, against the prior and the other brethren of the same church have no force; and that he should not omit to restore to their former state what was done after the first appeal to the prejudice of their rights. We therefore command and direct your discretion by apostolic letters that, if the aforesaid archbishop delays to carry out what we command within the prescribed period, you shall put it into execution, setting aside every delay and appeal; notwithstanding any letters which may appear to have been obtained from the Apostolic See to the prejudice of truth and justice.

If all of you cannot be present for carrying this out, nevertheless two of you shall execute it.

[Col. 1500B] Given at Verona, on the Kalends of March.

## CXXII. Takes the Church of St Peter of Bologna under protection and confirms its goods and rights. (Verona, March 2.)

[SAVIOLI, *Annali Bolognesi*, II, 149.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons GERARD, archdeacon, HUBERT, archpriest, and the canons of the Church of St Peter of Bologna, present and future, canonically appointed: in perpetuity.

Whenever a request is made of us which is recognized to accord with reason and propriety, it is fitting that we grant it willingly and bestow suitable assistance upon the petitioners’ desires. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just supplications; and, after the example of our predecessor Alexander, pope of happy memory, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present document, the aforesaid Church of St Peter at Bologna, in which you are dedicated to divine service. We decree that whatever possessions and goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the grants of pontiffs, the gifts of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with the Lord’s help acquire, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have determined [Col. 1500D] to specify the following by name:
