The place itself in which the aforesaid church is situated, with its appurtenances; the church of St John the Baptist; the church of St Mary of Montovallo; the church of St James, with the hospital situated in the place of St Rofillus; the hospital beside the cross of Prestribardo; the hospital at Ucula; the church of St Michael of the middle market; the church of St Donatus; the church of St Mary Magdalene at Talnisi; the church of St Giles beside the Savena; the church of St Peter and Savinus at Castaniolo; the church of St Michael of Argelata and the parish church of Medicina; the church of St Mary of the Vineyards, the church of St Lawrence, and the church of St Michael which are in Medicina, with all the appurtenances of the aforesaid churches; the churches of St Thomas and St Mary at Garda, and of St John at Fontana; [Col. 1501A] also the land, with and without houses, around the church of St Peter of your bishopric—namely that lying to the south, west, and north within the city wall, in the place called the Hospital, and outside the wall as far as the road of St Thomas the Apostle, and from the square leading to the same church as far as the three-way crossroads called Avesa; all the demesne which you have and hold; likewise three parts of the tithes of your entire parish, namely of St Peter’s bishopric, with all first-fruits, offerings of the living and the dead, and whatever is offered in your holy episcopal church, whether placed upon the altar or upon the pavement; and the tithes of the whole parish of Buida.

Furthermore, as G., bishop of Bologna of good memory, released you from the burden of expenses which you used to incur in going to and returning from Ravenna for the synod, as is known to be contained in the authentic document made on that matter, we release you by apostolic authority and decree that both you and your successors shall remain released from it in the future. We also enact by this present decree that the liberties and immunities reasonably granted to your church by kings, princes, and other persons, ecclesiastical as well as secular, and the ancient and reasonable customs hitherto observed, shall remain whole and unimpaired. When a general interdict of the land is in force, you may celebrate divine offices behind closed doors, excluding the excommunicated and interdicted, without ringing bells and in a subdued voice.

We therefore decree that no person may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations whatsoever; but that all things be preserved whole and unimpaired for the benefit in every way of those uses for whose governance or support they were granted, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the bishop of Bologna. If, therefore, in the future any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should rashly attempt to act against it, let him, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by due satisfaction, [Col. 1501D] be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know that he is guilty before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred Body and Blood of God and our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve their rights to that place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that here they may receive the fruit of good works and before the strict Judge may find the rewards of eternal peace. Amen.

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Peter de Bona, priest-cardinal of the title of St Susanna, have subscribed. I, Laborans, priest-cardinal of St Mary in Trastevere, of the title of Callistus, have subscribed. [Col. 1502A] I, Pandulf, priest-cardinal of the title of the Twelve Apostles, have subscribed. I, Melchior, priest-cardinal of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius, have subscribed. I, Adelard, priest-cardinal of the title of St Marcellus, have subscribed. I, James, deacon-cardinal of St Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed. I, Gerard, deacon-cardinal of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Roland, deacon-cardinal of St Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Peter, deacon-cardinal of St Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Rodulf, deacon-cardinal of St George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

[Col. 1502B] Given at Verona, through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixth day before the Nones of March, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1187 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban III.

## CXXIII. Privilege for the abbey of St Ghislain. (Verona, March 7.)

[REIFFENBERG, *Monuments du Hainaut*, VIII, 401.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son LAMBERT, abbot of the monastery of St Ghislain, and to his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: in perpetuity.

Those who choose the religious life ought fittingly to have apostolic protection at hand, lest an assault of any rash person either draw them back from their purpose or, God forbid, weaken the strength of their sacred religious life. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions and, after the example of Lucius, our predecessor of happy memory, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and of ourselves, and fortify by the privilege of this present document, the aforesaid monastery of St Ghislain, in which you are dedicated to divine service. First, indeed, we decree that the monastic order known to have been instituted in that place according to God and the Rule of St Benedict shall be observed there inviolate for all time. Moreover, whatever possessions and goods that monastery now [Col. 1502D] justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter, by the grants of pontiffs, the gifts of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other just means, with the Lord’s help acquire, shall remain firm and unimpaired for you and your successors; among which we have determined to specify the following by name:

The place itself in which the aforesaid monastery is situated, with all its appurtenances; the village of Hornut, with its appurtenances; in the village of Logia (*Slogia*, ed.), the demesne court and a ploughland of arable land, with courts and all tithes both of that land itself and of all the fiefs of the same village; the tithes which you possess in the lands of Saint Peter; the tithe from Hugh’s vineyard; the hamlet called Ultra Montes, with its appurtenances, and the church of that place [Col. 1503A] with its dependencies of Harminiac and Beweniis; the tithe from Curte and from the lands of Saint Landelin; at Novella, one ploughland of arable land; a fourth part of the village of Blelgiis, with its appurtenances and jurisdiction; in the village called Wamia, the allod of Gonther and his son Aegidius, of Cing, and the land of Hugh of Aengien, together with other lands, crofts, revenues, meadows, and woods; a part of the village of Darni, with the village and jurisdiction; the village of Vaherias and the demesne court, free from every advocacy and tithe; the church which you possess from the church of Saint Gaugeric at an annual rent of one hundred solidi in the money of Cambrai; in the village of Chavren, the demesne court with lands, waters, meadows, woods, and crofts, and a portion of the tithe, free from every lordship [Col. 1503B] and divided from the other portions; in the village called Harcheis, three fertons by the weight of Flanders, which the church of Alne owes for the land of Heluidis; at Resbaco, the demesne court and three parts of the whole allod, in lands, woods, waters, meadows, and revenues, with jurisdiction; at Roncherias, six marks of silver by the weight of Cologne, which the church of Cambron owes as an annual rent for the lands and altar of that place and for the chapel of Herieriponte; the altar of Cella, with its dependencies Hornut and Quaternio; the church of Durno, with the dependencies Blelgiis, Hercana, Astices, and Slogio; the church of Villari, with its dependencies Harminiac and Bewengiis; the church of Wamia, with its appurtenances; Altregium, with the chapel of the village, with its appurtenances [Col. 1503C]; at Imbrecies, the demesne court and lands, with meadows and waters; two parts of the common allod; the altar of Bossut, with its appurtenances; the altar of Baldurno, with its dependency Vilerot; the altars of Elignies and Tumaïdes; the chapel of Ramigniis, with its appurtenances; Abecias, with its dependencies Belehi, Molembais, Popiola, Piereweiz, and others, with their appurtenances; likewise, the altars conferred upon you by Nicholas, of good memory, formerly bishop of Cambrai, and confirmed by his privileges: Harcies, with its dependencies Grand-Ecclesia, Strabursia, and the chapel of Equicampus; the altar of Blatum; the chapel of Wieres; the altar of Tulin, with its dependency Henin; the altar of Hunchignies; the altar of Hersella; the altar of Rascengien; the altar of [Col. 1503D] Humberges; the altar of Goy, with land and its other dependencies; the altar of Lovigniis, with its dependencies Dolziis and the chapel of Squeri; the chapel of Delfait and the chapel of Herieriponte; in the village of Alemannis, the demesne court and the tithe of that court and of the land belonging to that same court, in lands, vineyards, meadows, woods, and the chapel for the household’s use; the demesne court and lands at Altregium, and shares in the common allod in lands, waters, meadows, woods, and revenues; the village of Bassecles with all its dependencies, and the administration of that same village, granted as alms to your monastery.

Moreover, no one shall presume to demand or extort from you tithes from your newly cleared lands, which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the sustenance of your animals [Col. 1504A]. You may also receive into conversion clerics or laymen fleeing the world, free and released from obligations, and retain them without any opposition. Furthermore, we prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in the same place, from being permitted to depart from that monastery; and no one shall dare to retain one who departs without letters of communion.

When a general interdict has been imposed upon the land, you may celebrate the divine offices with closed doors, excluding the interdicted and excommunicated, without ringing bells and in a subdued voice. We also grant that the burial-place of this house shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who choose to be buried there, unless they happen to be excommunicated [Col. 1504B] or under interdict, while preserving nevertheless the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken.

Upon the death of you, the present abbot of the same place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any cunning of usurpation or by force, except the person whom the brethren by common consent, or the greater part of the brethren of sounder judgment, in accordance with God and the Rule of blessed Benedict, shall provide to be elected. We hold valid the customs, including the ancient liberties and immunities, reasonably granted to your monastery and church and hitherto observed; and we decree that they shall remain unimpaired in future times. Furthermore, we forbid anyone to dare to pronounce against you or your churches a sentence of excommunication, suspension, or interdict without manifest and reasonable cause [Col. 1504C].

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid monastery, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all shall be preserved whole and unimpaired, for the benefit in every way of the uses for which they were granted, namely, the governance and support of those concerned, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical justice of the diocesan bishops. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person, knowing this page of our constitution, should presume rashly to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment [Col. 1504D] for the wrong committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that monastery, may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that they may receive here the fruit of good deeds and find before the strict Judge the rewards of eternal peace. Amen, amen, amen.

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, title of Saint Callistus. [Col. 1505A] I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the title of the Twelve Apostles. I, Major, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, title of Pammachius. I, Henry, bishop of Albano. I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina. I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Roland, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Radulf, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil [Col. 1505B].

Given at Verona, through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the Nones of March, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1186 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban III.

### CXXIV. He receives the monastery of Saint Saviour of Trebbia under protection and confirms its goods and rights.  
*(Verona, 12 March.)*

[CAMPI, *History of Piacenza*, II, 370.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot of Saint Saviour of Trebbia and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular [Col. 1505C] life: in perpetuity.

The authority of the Apostolic See, over which, though unworthy, we preside, admonishes us to labour with prudent care for the welfare of all churches, and to afford them apostolic protection lest they be exposed to the plundering or harassment of evil men. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your just petitions; and, following the example of Pope Alexander, our predecessor of happy memory, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church of Saint Saviour of Trebbia, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this document. First, we decree that the monastic order which is known to have been established in that place in accordance with God, the Rule of blessed Benedict, and the institution of the Pulsanese [Col. 1505D] order, shall be observed there perpetually. Furthermore, whatever possessions or goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire, by grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have judged it proper to specify the following by their own names.

The place itself in which the aforesaid church is situated, with all its appurtenances; the bridge of Trebbia and the fishing-right in that water from Goxolengo as far as that same bridge; and the two channels drawn from the bed of that river, with their mills and revenues; the lands [Col. 1506A], vineyards, and houses which you possess in Gragnano; mills, houses, vineyards, and lands in Guxaligio; vineyards, lands, and houses in Arcellis; the land of Lorentiano; vineyards, lands, and houses of Passiano; lands of Castronovo; lands of Trejano; vineyards, lands, and houses of Momiano; lands of Baldinico; vineyards and lands at the stream Ceredano, as Berard, abbot of Saint Sixtus, confirmed to you in his own writing; lands of Caxali; lands and woods of Calendasco; the wood of Sarmada; lands in Upper Campremaldo; lands in Mamogo; and lands in the court of Goxolenghi, a part of which the aforesaid abbot nevertheless confirmed to you; lands in the court of Valeria; lands in Valle; the land beside the Roman road, with its church and buildings; and we confirm to you by apostolic authority the houses which you possess in the city of Piacenza [Col. 1506B].

Moreover, no one shall presume to demand or extort from you tithes from the aforesaid newly cleared lands, cultivated by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the sustenance of your animals.

You may also receive into conversion clerics or laymen fleeing the world, free and released from obligations, and retain them without any opposition. Moreover, we prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in your house, from leaving that place without his abbot’s permission, except for the sake of a stricter religious observance; and no one shall dare to retain a departing brother without the security of letters of communion. They shall receive chrism, holy oil, consecrations of altars or churches, and the ordinations of clerics [Col. 1506C] to be promoted to sacred orders, from the diocesan bishop, provided that he is Catholic, enjoys the favour of the Apostolic See, and is willing to provide these things freely and without any improper demand. Otherwise, you may have recourse to whichever bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall grant what is requested. When a general interdict has been imposed upon the land, you may celebrate the divine offices with doors closed, excluding excommunicated and interdicted persons, without ringing bells and in a subdued voice. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of the same place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it through any cunning of usurpation, except the person whom the brethren by common consent, or the greater part of the brethren of sounder judgment, shall provide to be elected in accordance with the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Benedict [Col. 1506D].

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may, etc.

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Henry, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna, have subscribed. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, title of Saint Callistus, have subscribed. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the title of the Twelve Apostles, have subscribed. I, Melchior, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, title of Pammachius. [Col. 1507A] I, Adelard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, James, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Roland, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Radulf, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Ides of March, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1186 of the Lord’s Incarnation—[Note: [Col. 1507D] 1187 from the Nativity.]—and in the second year of the pontificate [Col. 1507B] of Lord Pope Urban III.

### CXXV. To the master and brethren of the cross-bearers of the Hospital of Bologna—he approves their order.  
*(Verona, 26 March.)*

[MANSI, *Councils*, XXII, 499.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons BEN., master, and the cross-bearing brethren of the house of the Hospital of Bologna, present and future, living the common life: in perpetuity.

Since your predecessor, son prior, received from Alexander, pope of blessed memory and our predecessor, the foundation stone for building a church in the territory [Col. 1507C] of Bologna, where your house is now known to have been built, we, not being moved by your petitions, receive into the right and property of blessed Peter and under our protection that same church, in which you are dedicated to the service of God and of the poor, and strengthen it by the privilege of this document. We decree that whatever possessions or goods your same church together with the Hospital now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire through grants of popes, gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have judged it proper to specify the following by their own names: the place itself in which the aforesaid hospital and church are situated [Col. 1507D], with all its appurtenances: etc.

Moreover, no one shall presume to demand or extort from you tithes from your newly cleared lands, which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the sustenance of your animals.

You may also receive into conversion and the service of Christ’s poor persons fleeing the world who are free and released from obligations, and retain them without any opposition.

But we forbid any ecclesiastical or secular person to dare to introduce anyone into your house or violently expel any of your brethren from it. Clerics also who have been ordained and admitted to [Col. 1508A] your houses shall be compelled to render obedience to no one other than you, son prior. Furthermore, we prohibit anyone from subjecting you or your houses to interdict or excommunication without manifest and reasonable cause and lawful citation. By this present page we decree that no prelate of churches shall dare to demand or extort anything from your houses except a pound of wax, while preserving those rents which are now established, with the bishops’ consent, to be received annually in certain of your houses.

Likewise, we have considered it right to grant you that, in your houses where so many brethren constantly reside and where a church is necessary, you may erect oratories [Col. 1508B] and establish cemeteries. We decree that their burial shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who choose to be buried there, unless they happen to be excommunicated or under interdict, while preserving nevertheless the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken.

You shall receive chrism, holy oil, dedications of churches, the ordinations of clerics to be promoted to sacred orders, and the other ecclesiastical sacraments from whichever Catholic bishop you prefer, who, supported by our authority, shall provide what is requested.

As a token that your same house belongs especially to blessed Peter, you shall pay twelve imperial [coins] to us and our successors each year [Col. 1508C].

Therefore we decree that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church and hospital, take away its possessions, retain what has been taken, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all shall be kept intact for the benefit in every way of the uses for which they were granted, namely, the governance and support of those concerned, without prejudice to the authority of the Apostolic See. If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in future, knowing this page of our constitution, should attempt rashly to act against it, then, after a second or third warning, unless he corrects his offence by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the dignity of his power [Col. 1508D] and honour; let him know himself guilty before the divine judgment for the wrong committed; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ the Redeemer; and at the last judgment let him be subject to severe vengeance. But upon all who preserve the rights of that place may the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ rest, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find before the strict Judge the rewards of peace. Amen.

**TO YOU, O LORD, I HAVE LIFTED UP MY SOUL.**

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Henry, bishop of Albano. [Col. 1509A] I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. I, Peter, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of Saint Mary across the Tiber, title of Saint Callistus. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the title of the Twelve Apostles. I, Melchior, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, title of Pammachius. I, Adelard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus. I, James, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Roland, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. [Col. 1509B] I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Rad[ulf; perhaps Radulf], cardinal deacon of Saint Gregory at the Golden Veil.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Moses, canon of the Lateran, acting in place of the chancellor, on the seventh day before the Kalends of April, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1187 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban III.

### CXXVI. He commands B[aldwin], archbishop of Canterbury and legate of the Apostolic See, to abandon construction of a new church, which the monks of Canterbury have complained to him would be detrimental to them.  
*(Verona, 8 May.)*

[TWISDEN, *Histories of English Writers*, I, 1318.]

[Col. 1509C]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother B., archbishop of Canterbury and legate of the Apostolic See: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Our beloved sons, the prior and certain brethren, monks of the church entrusted to you, came into our presence and represented that the church which you have begun to build will bring so great a loss upon themselves and that church that, unless its construction is discontinued, their aforesaid church will suffer a grievous loss of its dignity and standing. Since indeed, by God’s grace, you are learned and have long lived in religion, you cannot be ignorant—as we do not believe you are ignorant—how, because of scandal, even good works must sometimes be refrained from [Col. 1509D]. Therefore, wishing carefully to provide that no matter for contention should remain between you and your brethren, since persons devoted to disputes cannot suitably attend to divine service, by the counsel and deliberation of our brethren we admonish, command, and strictly enjoin your fraternity: until, after the case has been examined, we determine what ought to be done concerning that building, you shall, setting aside pretext, objection, and appeal, desist from constructing that new church and from instituting canons, and also from the collection of the fraternity which you are said to have established in support of that work, notwithstanding other letters obtained from the Apostolic See. If anything is attempted contrary to this our prohibition [Col. 1510A], we annul it by apostolic authority.

Given at Verona, on the eighth day before the Ides of May.

### CXXVII. To bishops, abbots, and other prelates of churches established throughout England, he communicates the foregoing letter to the archbishop of Canterbury.  
*(Verona, 9 May.)*

[Ibid., 1319.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brethren the bishops and beloved sons the abbots and other prelates of churches established throughout England: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since our beloved sons, the prior and brethren of the Church of Canterbury, complain that they will suffer serious losses from the construction of a new church [Col. 1510B] which our venerable brother, the archbishop of Canterbury and legate of the Apostolic See, has newly begun outside Canterbury, we, wishing as our office requires to provide for their right, have, after deliberation with our brethren, strictly commanded the archbishop himself not to proceed with constructing the aforesaid new church or instituting canons until, once the case has been examined, we determine what should be done in this matter. Therefore we command and enjoin your whole body that you shall in no way admit into your parishes, until the case is decided, the fraternity or preaching which the aforesaid archbishop has newly established on the occasion of that church; nor shall you allow preachers, if any have been appointed for this purpose, to preach in those parishes [Col. 1510C] or seek benefactions from the faithful. Rather, setting aside the obstacle of appeal, you shall compel them by ecclesiastical coercion and our authority to desist from these things.

Given at Verona, on the seventh day before the Ides of May.

### CXXVIII. He reproaches B[aldwin], archbishop of Canterbury, because he has not carried out his commands, issued on the first day of March.  
*(Verona, perhaps May.)*

[Ibid.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to B., archbishop of Canterbury and legate of the Apostolic See: greeting and apostolic blessing.

The greater your religious standing, integrity, and reputation, the more your dignity is diminished whenever you resist an apostolic command, to which you are bound in all things to submit with ready devotion. For in other letters we commanded you that, if, after the appeal to us lodged by our beloved sons, the prior and brethren of that church, or after that prior with certain of his brethren set out on the journey to come to the Apostolic See, you had done anything concerning the condition of your church, in persons or property, to their prejudice, you should restore it to its former state. We are therefore not without reason astonished that, as has been made known to us, you have been unwilling to carry out our command, since you know that both those who appeal and those who come to the Roman Church ought to suffer no impairment of their position until the dispute is examined [Col. 1511A].

Believing, however, that on this occasion you ought to do what you have hitherto neglected, by these repeated letters we command and strictly enjoin your fraternity that, setting aside delay and appeal, you shall not delay to restore to its former state whatever you have done concerning the position of the prior and brethren of that church, in persons or property, to their prejudice, after they appealed to us or after the prior and certain of his men set out on the journey to come to us; and henceforth cease to harass them in persons or property contrary to the order of law. But if you do not perform this within fifteen days after receiving these letters, we have committed its execution, with appeal removed, to our beloved sons, the abbots of Battle, Faversham, and [Col. 1511B] Saint Augustine’s, Canterbury; so that, if all are unwilling or unable to take part in carrying this out, two of them shall nevertheless carry it out.

### CXXIX. He rebukes the abbots of Battle, Faversham, and Saint Augustine’s because they have neglected his commands.  
*(Verona, perhaps May.)*

[Ibid., p. 1495.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbots of Battle, Faversham, and Saint Augustine’s, Canterbury: greeting and apostolic blessing.

We take it as exceedingly grave and burdensome [Col. 1511C] that our venerable brother, the archbishop of Canterbury and legate of the Apostolic See, acted against our beloved prior and his brethren after their appeal, disregarding the reverence due to the Apostolic See; and that, as we have learned, he was unwilling either at our command or at your admonition to undo what he had done. It is pleasing to us that, although you proceeded far too sluggishly in executing the mandate we gave you in this matter, yet it would have pleased us much more had you so executed the tenor of our command that we were not compelled to send you repeated letters on the same matter. But because we cannot remain unmoved by the burdens and harassments of that prior and his brethren, and because we are unwilling to tolerate uncorrected what is clearly known to have been done to their prejudice, not without contempt [Col. 1511D] for the Apostolic See, we have issued a repeated mandate and command to the aforesaid archbishop: whatever he attempted concerning the position of that prior and his brethren, in persons or property, to their prejudice, after they appealed to us or after the same prior and certain of his men set out upon the journey to come into our presence, he must, with delay and pretext removed, restore to its former state, and henceforth cease to harass them in persons or property contrary to the order of law.

Therefore, lest we seem to write so often in vain concerning the same business, by apostolic letters we command and strictly enjoin your belovedness that, if the aforesaid archbishop does not fulfil our command within fifteen days after receiving our letters, you shall effectively execute it, with objection, delay, and appeal likewise set aside. Take care that you do not seem in this matter to yield more to him than to us, because we could not but be moved against you if, through anyone’s favour or influence, you neglect to obey apostolic commands and we are compelled to extend our hand to correct your disobedience [Col. 1512A]. Moreover, if all of you cannot take part in executing these things, two of you shall nevertheless execute them.

### CXXX. Privilege for the Church of Pistoia.  
[Note: [Col. 1511] For a copy of this bull, of which only the subscriptions are given here, see *Patrologia*, vol. CLXXIX, under Innocent II, year 1134, 12 Kalends of January.]  
*(Verona, 21 May.)*

[ZACHARIA, *Anecdota of the Middle Ages*, 244.]

[Col. 1512B]

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church, subscribed. I, Henry, bishop of Albano, subscribed. I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina, subscribed. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri, subscribed. I, Peter Debono, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Susanna. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Callistus, subscribed. I, Pandulf, cardinal priest of the title of the Twelve Apostles. I, Melchior, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, title of Pammachius. I, Adelard, cardinal priest of the title of Saint Marcellus, subscribed. [Col. 1512C] I, Hyacinth, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Gratian, cardinal deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Roland, cardinal deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Peter, cardinal deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Radulf, cardinal deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Albert, cardinal priest and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the twelfth day before the Kalends of June, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1187 of the Lord’s Incarnation, in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban [Col. 1512D] III.

### CXXXI. Bull for the monastery of Blessed Mary of Voto.  
*(Verona, 22 May.)*

[*New Gallia Christiana*, XI, documents, 250.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons, the abbot of Blessed Mary of Caesarisburg and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life: for perpetual remembrance.

The authority of the Apostolic See, which we serve though unworthy, admonishes us to labour with prudent care for the welfare of all churches, and to impart apostolic protection to them lest they be exposed to the plundering or harassment of evil men [Col. 1513A]. Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we graciously assent to your petitions; and, after the model of Pope Alexander, our predecessor of happy memory, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church of Saint Mary of Caesarisburg, in which you are dedicated to divine service, and confirm it by the privilege of this document. First, we decree that the canonical order known to have been established in that church according to God, the Rule of blessed Augustine, and the institution of the brethren of Saint Victor, shall be observed there inviolably for all time. Furthermore, whatever possessions or goods that church now justly and canonically possesses, or may in future acquire by grants of popes [Col. 1513B], gifts of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, through the Lord’s favour, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have judged it proper to specify the following by their own names:

The place itself, namely the island of Ulmus, upon which the aforesaid church is situated, with all its appurtenances; Novavilla, with all its appurtenances; [lacuna]; the land of Master John in Coqueurdrevilla; three parts of the mill of Ihioul in the same village; [lacuna]; the monastery of Saint Helier on the island of Jersey, as that monastery was granted to your church by Rotrou, archbishop of Rouen, of good memory, and confirmed by the authentic document both of him and of Walter, [Col. 1513C] our venerable brother and his successor, with the consent of the prince of the land, in whose alms [lacuna]; the holding which Robert the knight gave you at Caesarisburg [lacuna]; no one shall presume to demand or extort from you tithes from lands which you cultivate by your own hands or at your own expense, or from the sustenance of your animals. You may also receive into conversion clerics or laymen fleeing the world, free and released from obligations, and retain them without any opposition. Furthermore, we prohibit any of your brethren, after making profession in the same place, from departing that place without his abbot’s permission; and no one shall dare to retain a departing brother without the security of letters of communion. When a general interdict has been imposed upon the land [Col. 1513D], you may celebrate the divine offices with doors closed, excluding excommunicated and interdicted persons, without ringing bells and in a subdued voice. In the parish churches which you possess, you may choose priests and present them to the diocesan bishop; if they are suitable, the bishop shall entrust the care of souls to them, so that they must answer to him in spiritual matters, but to you in temporal matters. We also forbid anyone to presume to burden or harass you, without manifest and reasonable cause, in presenting priests or arranging churches. Furthermore, we prohibit anyone from giving personally, or otherwise alienating, churches, lands, or any benefice conferred upon your church without the consent of the entire chapter, or of its greater and sounder part [Col. 1514A]. If any grants or alienations have been made otherwise than stated, we decree them void. We also forbid anyone within the parishes of your churches to presume to build a church or oratory without the assent of the diocesan bishop and yourselves, without prejudice, nevertheless, to the privileges of the Roman Church. We further prohibit anyone from presuming to pronounce sentences of excommunication or interdict against you or your churches without manifest and reasonable cause.

Moreover, we decree that all liberties, reasonable customs, and immunities which the illustrious king of the English, Henry, and the Empress Matilda, his mother of good memory, advocate and foundress of the aforesaid church, or their successors, have bestowed upon you and your church by pious grant and established by their authentic documents, shall remain secure and unimpaired. Furthermore, we utterly forbid new and unlawful exactions to be made by archbishops or bishops, archdeacons or deans, or any other ecclesiastical persons. For chrism, holy oil, consecrations of churches, or sacraments, no one shall dare to demand anything from you, whether merely on the pretext of custom or in any other way. Furthermore, we decree that the burial-place of the same house shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion and last will of those who choose to be buried there, unless they happen to be excommunicated or under interdict, while preserving nevertheless the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead [Col. 1514C] are taken. Upon the death of you, the present abbot of the same place, or of any of your successors, no one shall be set over it by any cunning of usurpation or by force, except the person whom the brethren unanimously, or the part of the brethren of sounder judgment, shall provide to be elected in accordance with the fear of God and the Rule of blessed Augustine.

We therefore decree that it shall be lawful for no person whatsoever rashly to disturb the aforesaid church, or to take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it by any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole, and be of benefit in every way for the uses for which they were granted—for the governance and support of those concerned—saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, [Col. 1514D] any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowingly, should rashly attempt to act against this page of our constitution, after a second or third warning, unless he correct his fault by suitable satisfaction, let him be deprived of the rank of his power or honour, and recognize himself as answerable before the Lord’s judgment for the iniquity committed. [lacuna] But upon all who preserve their rights for the same place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, etc. [lacuna]

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Henry, bishop of Albano. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia. I, Peter of Bono, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Susanna. [Col. 1515A] I, Laborans, priest-cardinal of Saint Mary beyond the Tiber, of the title of Saint Callistus. I, Rainerius, priest-cardinal of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius. I, Hyacinthus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Gratian, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian. I, Roland, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Portico. I, Peter, cardinal-deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison. I, Radulph, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman [Col. 1515B] Church, on the eleventh day before the Kalends of June, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1187 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban III. (Under a lead seal.)

### CXXXII. He orders that alienations made by the bishops of Bologna to the detriment of the Church be void.  
*(Verona, 25 May.)*

[SAVIOLI, *Annals of Bologna*, II, II, 151.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother the bishop of Bologna: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Although unworthy, the care and solicitude of all churches have been entrusted to us by divine disposition [Col. 1515C], so that we must both attend vigilantly to their advancement and, with pastoral zeal, safeguard them from loss. Therefore, venerable brother bishop in Christ, pursuing the duty of the office entrusted to us and giving willing assent to your just requests, we decree that alienations, leases, enfeoffments, and any other unlawful contracts made by your predecessors to the prejudice of your church shall be without force; and we grant you free authority lawfully to revoke them.

Therefore let no person infringe this page of our constitution or, with rash boldness, act contrary to it. But if anyone presumes to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of the blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

[Col. 1515D] Given at Verona, in the year 1187 of the Lord’s Incarnation, on the eighth day before the Kalends of June, in the second year of the pontificate.

### CXXXIII. He decrees that the Order of Saint Benedict shall be preserved for ever in the monastery of Admont; he also confirms all its possessions and provides for the immunity of the place.  
*(Verona, 26 May.)*

[PEZ, *Treasury of Anecdotes*, III, III, 674.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons ISENRIC, abbot of the monastery of Saint Blaise called Admont, and his brethren, present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

[Col. 1516A] The authority of our office admonishes and invites us to labour for the condition of the churches and, with the Lord’s saving assistance, to provide for their peace and tranquillity. For it is recognized as worthy and fitting to propriety that we, who by the Lord’s ordering have been appointed to govern them, should both defend them from the wickedness of evil men and fortify them with the patronage of blessed Peter and of the Apostolic See.

Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, we mercifully assent to your just requests; and, following the example of our predecessors of blessed memory, Paschal, Innocent, Lucius, Alexander, and Lucius, Roman pontiffs, we receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid monastery of Saint Blaise, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. [Col. 1516B] First, indeed, we establish that the monastic order which is recognized as instituted in the same monastery according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict shall there be observed inviolate for all time.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods the same monastery now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, the Lord granting it, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following in their proper terms: from the gift of Gebehard, archbishop of Salzburg, of blessed memory and founder of the same monastery, in the Valley of Admont [Col. 1516C], the estate of the Church of Saint Blaise, etc., as in the bull of Alexander III for the same monastery.

Further, desiring with paternal care to provide for your peace and tranquillity, we forbid by apostolic authority that, within the enclosures of your places or granges, anyone should presume by any rashness to commit violence, robbery, or theft; set fire; seize a person; or kill.

We decree, therefore, etc., as in the cited passage.

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Henry, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri [Col. 1516D], have subscribed. I, Peter of Bono, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Susanna, have subscribed. I, Laborans, priest-cardinal of Saint Mary beyond the Tiber, of the title of Saint Callistus, have subscribed. I, Pandulf, priest-cardinal of the title of the Twelve Apostles, have subscribed. I, Melchior, priest-cardinal of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius, have subscribed. I, Adelard, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Hyacinthus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed. I, Gratian, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. [Col. 1517A] I, Roland, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal-deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Radulph, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the seventh day before the Kalends of June, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1187 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban III.

### CXXXIV. Bull of Urban III issued to the nuns of Saint Grata in 1187. From the archive of M. S. Grata. He receives the convent of Saint Grata at Bergamo under protection and confirms its possessions.  
*(Verona, 2 June.)*

[LUPI, *Diplomatic Codex of Bergamo*, II, 1379.]

[Col. 1517B]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, EUGENIA, abbess of the monastery of Saint Grata, and her sisters, present and future, professing the regular life: for perpetual remembrance.

To prudent virgins who, beneath the religious habit, continually prepare themselves by works of holiness to go out to meet the Bridegroom, we ought to grant apostolic protection, lest an attack of any rashness either turn them aside from their purpose or, which God forbid, impair the strength of holy religion.

Therefore, beloved daughters in [Col. 1517C] the Lord, we mercifully assent to your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church of Saint Grata, in which you are devoted to divine service; and we strengthen it by the patronage of this present writing. First, indeed, we establish that the monastic order recognized as instituted in the same church according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict shall there be observed for all time.

Moreover, whatever possessions and goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire, by grant of pontiffs, generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, the Lord granting it, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and those [Col. 1517D] who succeed you. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following in their proper terms:

The very place in which the aforesaid church is situated, with all its appurtenances; the church of Saint Gervasius, with the estate of Saranica and its other appurtenances; the church of Saint Mary of Calventiano with its appurtenances; possessions at Albenio; the church of Saint Michael with its appurtenances, confirmed to you by the authentic writing of Ambrose II, of blessed memory. Concerning, moreover, your newly cultivated lands, etc. All as in the bull of 1186 reported above, no. 59.

In the circle: “TO YOU, O LORD, I HAVE LIFTED UP MY SOUL.”

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. [Col. 1518A] I, Henry, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri, have subscribed. I, Pederbonus, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Susanna, have subscribed. I, Laborans, priest-cardinal of Saint Mary beyond the Tiber, of the title of Saint Callistus, have subscribed. I, Pandulf, priest-cardinal of the title of the Twelve Apostles, have subscribed. I, Melchior, priest-cardinal of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius, have subscribed. I, Adelard, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Jac[inthus], cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin [Col. 1518B], have subscribed. I, Gratian, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Roland, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal-deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Radulf, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Nones of June, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1187 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban III.

### CXXXV. He receives the convent of Saint Euphemia at Modena under protection and confirms its possessions and privileges.  
*(Verona, 2 June.)*

[MURATORI, *Italian Antiquities*, III, 207.]

[Col. 1518C]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved daughters in Christ, MARIA, abbess of Saint Euphemia of Modena, and her sisters, present and future, professing the monastic life: for ever.

The Apostolic See ought to provide protection for prudent virgins who, under the religious habit, with lamps lit, continually prepare themselves by works of holiness to go out to meet the Bridegroom, lest an attack of any rashness [Col. 1518D] either turn them aside from their purpose or, which God forbid, weaken the strength of sacred religion. Therefore, beloved daughters in Christ, we mercifully assent to your just requests and receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid church of Saint Euphemia, in which you are devoted to divine service, and strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing.

First, indeed, we establish that the monastic order recognized as instituted in that place according to God and the Rule of blessed Benedict shall there be observed inviolate for all time. Accordingly, whatever possessions and goods the same church now justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, the offerings [Col. 1519A] of the faithful, or other lawful means, the Lord granting it, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following in their proper terms:

The very place in which the aforesaid church is situated, with all its appurtenances; the possessions which you have within and outside the city, namely houses, dwellings, and gardens with all appurtenances; the mill at the Gate of Bavaria; also the tithes of the bishop’s mill at the Gate of Cittanova; the *braida* formerly held by John Boniface; the vineyard *braida* held on lease by the lords of Marano; also the *braidae* and revenues which you have outside the city; the lands formerly held [Col. 1519B] by Hugolinus and the Cupbearer of Gisano; possessions and revenues which you have at Saint Peter of the Island and at Sulignano; tithes and revenues which you have at Sorbaria; and whatever you have at Vignola and in all other places. We also confirm to you by apostolic authority the tithes which your church has reasonably and peacefully held for forty years, our privileges thereby suffering no prejudice.

Moreover, no one shall presume to extort from you tithes of your newly cultivated lands which you cultivate by your own hands or resources, or of the produce of your animals. You may also receive into conversion persons fleeing from the secular world who are free and absolved, and retain them without any opposition. [Col. 1519C] Furthermore, we forbid any of your sisters, after making profession in the same place, to leave that place without the licence of her abbess, except for the sake of a stricter religious life; and no one shall dare retain a sister who has departed without a guarantee in letters from the community.

When a general interdict of the land has been imposed, you may celebrate the divine offices with doors shut, excommunicated and interdicted persons excluded, bells not rung, and the voice subdued. By apostolic authority we also forbid anyone, without manifest and reasonable cause, to pronounce against you or your church a sentence of excommunication, suspension, or interdict, or to impose new and unlawful exactions upon you or your people.

We likewise decree that the burial-place of that locality shall be free, so that no one may oppose the devotion [Col. 1519D] and last will of those who have resolved to be buried there, unless they are excommunicated or interdicted; nevertheless, the rights of those churches from which the bodies of the dead are taken are preserved. Upon the death of you, the present abbess of the same church, or of any one of your successors, no one shall be placed there by any deceitful device or violence, except the woman whom the sisters, by common consent or by the sounder counsel of the greater part of the sisters, in the fear of God and according to the Rule of blessed Benedict, shall provide to be elected.

We decree, therefore, that no one, etc., saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the canonical right of the diocesan bishop. If, therefore, any person in the future, etc.

[Col. 1520A] Fare well.

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church, have subscribed. I, Henry, bishop of Albano, have subscribed. I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina, have subscribed. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri, have subscribed. I, Peter of Bon[o], priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Susanna, have subscribed. I, Laborans, priest-cardinal of Saint Mary beyond the Tiber, of the title of Saint Callistus, have subscribed. I, Pandulf, priest-cardinal of the title of the Twelve Apostles, have subscribed. I, Melchior, priest-cardinal of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius, have subscribed. [Col. 1520B] I, Adelard, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Hyacinthus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed. I, Gratian, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Roland, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Portico, have subscribed. I, Peter of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Radulf, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, [Col. 1520C] on the second day before the Nones of June, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1187 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban III.

A lead bull is suspended.

### CXXXVI. He confirms certain privileges of the Premonstratensian Order.  
*(Verona, 10 June.)*

[LE PAIGE, *Premonstratensian Library*, 639.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HUGH, abbot of Prémontré, his co-abbots, and the brethren, present and future, to be regularly instituted for ever: greeting and apostolic blessing.

[Col. 1520D] Since by the office of the apostolate entrusted to us by God we are bound to all the faithful of God in advancing their just petitions, we ought all the more willingly to receive and make provision for the petitions of religious persons that concern their peace and tranquillity, because through their life the Church of Christ is adorned and those who remain in the world learn how they should walk in the right way through the works of God.

Now it has been represented to us through our venerable brother, the bishop of Evactunium, that certain members of the clergy or of the monastic order harass you with demands for tithes upon newly cultivated lands, on the ground that you grant to those persons from whom you receive forests to be cleared or other uncultivated places to be cultivated a rent or some portion of the fruits in return for ownership of the property; and that on this account they endeavour to infringe the freedom granted you by the Roman Church, which absolves you from paying tithes on newly cultivated lands. Since, therefore, such insistence has no basis in reason, we forbid by apostolic authority anyone to dare harass you on that account concerning tithes of your newly cultivated lands which you cultivate by your own hands or resources.

So that firm discipline may be maintained among you, we prohibit in this present chapter anyone within the cloister from presuming, contrary to canonical discipline, to appeal and thereby evade the correction of his prelates. Should anyone nevertheless attempt this, regular correction shall none the less be exercised upon him. For it is contrary both to order and to salvation [Col. 1521B] that one who, by his regular life, has subjected himself to the will of his prelate should be allowed, under pretext of appeal, to return to following his own inclination, so that licence for laxity may arise from the very source from which correction of faults ought to arise.

Moreover, because the need of religious persons to travel about should be removed, and because matters pertaining to salvation should be conferred upon them without difficulty, we have also thought fit to grant, out of apostolic kindness, that if your bishops either refuse or are willing to celebrate ordinations, and it happens that you have a visiting bishop whose office and authority are fully known to you, you may freely receive from him both orders and ecclesiastical sacraments—provided that he is such a man that your own bishop [Col. 1521C] need fear no prejudice to himself from this.

We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may infringe this page of our constitution or, with rash boldness, act contrary to it. If therefore anyone, etc.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the fourth day before the Ides of June, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1187 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the second year of the pontificate of our Lord Urban III.

### CXXXVII. He confirms the laws of the Premonstratensian Order.  
*(Verona, 30 June.)*

[Ibidem, 640.]

[Col. 1521D]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved sons HUGH, abbot of Prémontré, and the other abbots and canons of the Premonstratensian Order, present and future, professing the regular life, for ever.

Although unworthy, placed by the Lord’s ordering in the eminent watchtower of the Apostolic See, we are compelled to be solicitous for the condition of each person and are bound sincerely to embrace those things which advance religion and concern the adornment of virtues, so that the peace of religious persons may be secure from every disturbance and, fortified by apostolic protection, may remain unharmed by the yoke of worldly oppression.

Considering, therefore, how your religion and order, resplendent with abundant glory of merits and fragrant with the grace of holiness, extends its branches from sea to sea [Col. 1522A], we have thought fit to cherish the order itself and all houses of the same order with the protection of apostolic guardianship and to fortify them by this present privilege.

Therefore, beloved sons in the Lord, graciously acceding to your just petitions, after the example of Alexander and Lucius, Roman pontiffs of happy memory, our predecessors, we strengthen by apostolic authority and fortify by the privilege of this present writing all the regular institutions and regulations which you have made by common consent, or by the consent of the greater and sounder part, as set out below: namely, that the canonical order recognized as instituted in the Church of Prémontré [Col. 1522B], according to the Rule of blessed Augustine and the ordinance of Norbert, of revered memory, formerly founder of the Premonstratensian Order, and of his successors, in the white habit, shall be observed inviolate for ever in all churches of the same order. Likewise, the same books pertaining to the divine office shall be kept uniformly by all churches of the same order, etc., as they stand in the privilege or diploma of Lucius III, up to the matters that follow.

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church. I, Henry, bishop of Albano. I, Paul, bishop of Palestrina. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri. [Col. 1522C] I, Laborans, priest-cardinal of Saint Mary beyond the Tiber, of the title of Saint Callistus. I, Hyacinthus, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin. I, Radulph, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil.

Given at Verona, through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the day before the Kalends of July, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1187 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the second year of the pontificate of our Lord Pope Urban III.

### CXXXVIII. At the request of Bishop Gerard, he confirms the possessions of the Church of Bologna.  
*(Verona, 2 July.)*

[SAVIOLI, *Annals of Bologna*, II, II, 152.]

[Col. 1522D]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother GERARD, bishop of Bologna, and his successors to be appointed for ever.

The most holy Roman Church has always loved the Church of Bologna with a special prerogative and has endeavoured to honour it more devotedly than others. Hence we, who, though less adequate, have been placed in the watchtower of that same Church, love the aforesaid Church of Bologna with customary kindness and desire, venerable brother bishop, to grant willing assent to your just requests.

Therefore, brother bishop, embracing your person and the Church entrusted [Col. 1523A] to you in the full arms of charity, together with all its possessions, both lesser and greater, we specify: the estate of Prunarii; the estate of Vulpini, Mozularii, and Bonalbergiscatii; the estate in the place called Frefortese; the estate of Nucifatico; the estate of Nespulini; and other estates and lands in the same county. Besides this, all that we have in the same county from the patrimony of the noblewoman Countess Matilda, except the *Banno*; and whatever in the city of Bologna is adjudged, as hitherto and henceforth, on behalf of the Roman pontiff—as Anastasius, our predecessor of pious memory, is known, with the common counsel of his brethren, to have granted and leased in emphyteusis to Gerard, of blessed memory, formerly bishop of Bologna and your predecessor, upon receipt from him of one hundred pounds of *affortiati*, which Anastasius expended for the benefit [Col. 1523B] of the Roman Church.

We grant and lease these things to you and your successors, and through us to the Church of Bologna, by perpetual emphyteutic lease; and we confirm that lease by the page of this present writing. For this lease, you and your successors must pay to our successors two pounds of pure silver each year in the month of June.

Moreover, as was then established, we have thought fit to append to this present page that neither you nor any of your successors may in any way sell or alienate this [Col. 1523C] lease to any church or person, except to us and our successors. We and our successors, however, are bound to defend the aforesaid lease for you and your successors against every person. If either party neglects to perform what is his obligation, as stated above, he shall pay one hundred pounds of gold to the other party as a penalty, and the same lease shall remain indissoluble.

Therefore, let no person presume with rash boldness to act against this page of our lease or in any way to infringe it. But if anyone presumes to attempt this, let him know that he will incur the indignation of Almighty God and of His blessed apostles Peter and Paul.

I, Urban, bishop of the Catholic Church. [Col. 1523D] I, Henry, bishop of the Church of Albano, have subscribed. I, Peter of Bon[o], priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Susanna, have subscribed. I, Laborans, priest-cardinal of Saint Mary beyond the Tiber, of the title of Saint Callistus, have subscribed. I, Pandulf, priest-cardinal of the title of the Twelve Apostles, have subscribed. I, Melchior, priest-cardinal of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius, have subscribed. I, Adelard, priest-cardinal of the title of Saint Marcellus, have subscribed. I, Theobald, bishop of Ostia and Velletri, have subscribed. [Col. 1524A] I, Jacob, cardinal-deacon of Saint Mary in Cosmedin, have subscribed. I, Gratian, cardinal-deacon of Saints Cosmas and Damian, have subscribed. I, Peter, cardinal-deacon of Saint Nicholas in the Tullian Prison, have subscribed. I, Rodulph, cardinal-deacon of Saint George at the Golden Veil, have subscribed.

Given at Verona, through the hand of the priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the sixth day before the Nones of July, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1187 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban III.

### CXXXIX. Privilege for the canons of the Church of Treviso. *(Fragment.)*  
[Note: [Col. 1523] This bull is word for word the same as that which Pope Lucius III granted to the same canons on 1 October 1184. See *Patrology*, vol. CCI.]  
*(Verona, 25 August.)*

[UGHELLI, *Sacred Italy*, V, 535.]

[Col. 1524B]

[lacuna]

Given at Verona through the hand of Albert, priest-cardinal and chancellor of the Holy Roman Church, on the eighth day before the Kalends of September, in the fifth indiction, in the year 1187 of the Lord’s Incarnation, and in the second year of the pontificate of Lord Pope Urban.

### CXL. He directs [Peter], bishop-elect of Reggio, not to take an oath of allegiance to any mortal, except the archbishop [of Ravenna], upon receiving consecration, without a special apostolic mandate.  
*(Verona, 10 September.)*

[TIRABOSCHI, *Memoirs of Modena*, III, 101.]

[Col. 1524C] URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his beloved son [Peter], the bishop-elect of REGGIO: greeting and apostolic blessing.

Since we love you with paternal affection as a devoted son of the Church, we rejoice at your promotion and shall willingly bestow apostolic favour, wherever with God’s help we can, for your honour. But because you must strive and act so that at the beginning of your promotion you may begin with all your strength to advance the honour of God and of the most holy Apostolic See, we earnestly request, command, and enjoin you by virtue of obedience that, when, by the Lord’s grant, you receive the gift of consecration, you shall bind yourself by oath to no mortal without our special mandate, except perhaps to your archbishop; and that you shall be solicitous and zealous for our honour and that of the Church. Be assured that, if anyone at this time should proceed otherwise in rendering any allegiance, we should judge him not a son of the Church but its most manifest enemy.

Given at Verona, on the fourth day before the Ides of September.

### CXLI. Privilege for the Church of Cervia.  
*(Ferrara, September–October.)*

[FANTUZZI, *Monuments of Ravenna*, IV, 283.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother THEOBALD, bishop of Cervia, and his [Col. 1525A] successors canonically appointed for ever.

Although unworthy, placed by the Lord’s ordering in the watchtower of the Apostolic See, we are bound to love in fraternal charity our brother bishops, whether near or far away, and to strengthen the churches committed to their government against the assaults of evil men by the protection of apostolic guardianship.

Therefore, venerable brother Theobald, bishop in Christ, we assent to your just requests and, following in the footsteps of Lucius, our predecessor of happy memory, receive under the protection of blessed Peter and ourselves the aforesaid Church of Cervia, over which you are recognized, by God’s appointment, to preside; and we strengthen it by the privilege of this present writing. We establish that whatever possessions and goods the same church hereafter [Col. 1525B] justly and canonically possesses, or may hereafter acquire through the grant of pontiffs, the generosity of kings or princes, offerings of the faithful, or other lawful means, the Lord granting it, shall remain secure and unimpaired for you and your successors. Among these we have thought fit to specify the following in their proper terms:

The place commonly called Padule, with its salt-pans, lands, vineyards, meadows, pastures, hunting and fishing rights, extending from the stream called Pisatellus to the White Milestone, and from the *decimanus* to the sea. The parish church of Saint Vitalis, called Fiscalia, with chapels, tithes [lacuna] and its other appurtenances [Col. 1525C], extending from the embankment of Corlungo, the fishery ditch, and the stream of Rodaldo, running through the middle of the houses; on another side, through the middle of Verginese; on a third side, by Saint Elias, running through the middle of the holy lake; and on the fourth, the Po. Ten holdings of land, granted there by the men of the estate of Fiscalia, situated on the larger stream in the place called the Dead Channel and in other suitable places upon the said stream.

The holding formerly belonging to the parish church of Saint Thomas, with its port and other appurtenances. The holding formerly belonging to the parish church of Saint Peregrine, with tithes and its other appurtenances. D[ominus?] Arimund sold, from property situated at Saint Gervasius, the church of Saint Gervasius with its appurtenances, the bank of the mainland with its toll and other appurtenances, and the bank of the sea with the shore itself, toll, and [Col. 1525D] other appurtenances. The port with its toll and other appurtenances. In the territory of Ravenna, the castle of Pastellione with its appurtenances and the estate of Varignano. In the territory of Pesena, whatever Candolus has in the estate of Fabrice, and at Modale, Arturiano, and Montale called “of Laurentius”; and the two entire estates, Ceula and Assignano, which the monastery of Saint Mary of Mount Mauro holds from its church.

In the territory of Cornelia and the county of Imola, one entire castle called Plancaldoli, another called Vicli, and another called Saxum Gattarum, with all their appurtenances. In the territories of Fano and Pesaro, the castle called Monteriano with its district, court, and all appurtenances; and two [Col. 1526A] holdings of land between Marchisano and Ripalta, held by Ugolinus Guidoti; one holding at Lupara, held by Peter Sophie and Peter’s sons; one holding at Casale, held by the sons of Guidutius and Roger; one holding at Bulgum, held by Branchaleon; the church of Saint Andrew in the foul ditch in the city of Ravenna, with all its rights; and the riverbanks on land and sea, and ports. By apostolic authority we prohibit *tullia* or any impost contrary to ancient custom. We establish that these shall remain always under your authority and that of your successors, as they have remained down to modern times.

We also establish that within your diocese no one may presume, upon any pretext, to construct a new church [Col. 1526B] or oratory without your assent or that of your successors, saving nevertheless the privileges of the Roman pontiffs. Moreover, we ratify and confirm by apostolic authority the agreement made between you and your canons through the mediation of our venerable brother Ger[ard], archbishop of Ravenna—or reasonably made and accepted by both parties—as it is more fully contained in the writing of the same archbishop.

Upon the death of you, the present bishop of the same church, or of any of your successors, no one shall be put in charge there by any deceitful contrivance or violence, except the man whom the canons of the same church, by common consent or by the sounder counsel of the greater part of the canons, in the fear of God, shall provide to be elected.

[Col. 1526C] We decree, therefore, that no person whatsoever may rashly disturb the aforesaid church, take away its possessions, retain those taken away, diminish them, or harass it with any vexations; but that all things be preserved whole [lacuna] and be of benefit in every way for the uses for which they were granted for their governance and support, saving the authority of the Apostolic See and the due reverence owed to the archbishop of Ravenna.

If, therefore, any ecclesiastical or secular person in the future, knowingly, should rashly attempt to act against this page of our confirmation, after a second or third warning, unless he correct his fault by worthy satisfaction, let him be deprived of the rank of his power, honour, or dignity; let him recognize himself as answerable before the divine judgment for the iniquity committed [Col. 1526D]; let him be cut off from the most sacred body and blood of God and of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Redeemer; and let him be subject to divine vengeance at the last judgment. But upon all who, by authority, preserve their rights for the same place, may there be the peace of our Lord Jesus Christ, so that they may receive here the fruit of good action and find, before the strict Judge, the rewards of eternal peace.

I, Peter of Bono, cardinal priest of the title of St. Susanna, have subscribed. I, Laborans, cardinal priest of St. Mary across the Tiber, of the title of St. Callistus, have subscribed. I, Melchior, cardinal priest of Saints John and Paul, of the title of Pammachius, have subscribed. [Col. 1527A] I, Adelard, cardinal priest of the title of St. Marcellus, have subscribed. Etc., etc. . . .

CLXII. He sharply rebukes B[aldwin], Archbishop of Canterbury and legate of the Apostolic See, because he persists both in inflicting injuries upon the monks of Canterbury and in disregarding his commands. (Ferrara, 3 October.)

[TWISDEN, *Hist. Script.*, I, 1320.]

URBAN, bishop, servant of the servants of God, to his venerable brother B., Archbishop of Canterbury and legate of the Apostolic See: greeting and apostolic blessing.

If hitherto we have shown deference to your brotherhood and, although greatly provoked, have nevertheless not proceeded [Col. 1527B] to your detriment, the chief reason has been that, since you were a man of religion and of an order, and now have been raised in the Church of God to the summit of dignity, we believed that your heart would be recalled from oppressing the convent of the Church entrusted to you—if not out of reverence for us, which in this matter you seem, contrary to what becomes you, to have despised, then at least through fear of divine judgment. Indeed, we hoped, and in accordance with conscience believed, that once you had attained the eminent position which you hold in the English Church, you would become for others a pattern and example of that obedience and reverence which all ecclesiastical persons ought to show to the most holy Apostolic See. Therefore, at the beginning of both our promotion and yours, we took care to honour you in a manner hitherto unusual and new, [Col. 1527C] believing that, for the sake of our honour, we had found a most faithful man. But—what we do not say without grave astonishment—we have been disappointed in our expectations, and him whom we believed to be the faithful guardian of our honour we now find to be its assailant in our members.

For many times, for the peace of the brethren of the Church entrusted to you, we have sent you our letters, ordering you to cease troubling them and, at least out of reverence for us, not to disturb their rights. But you, not only in this matter but also in others—as common report everywhere proclaims of you almost universally—make light of our letters and of appeals lodged with the Apostolic See. We are ashamed to recount what you have done against them after their many appeals [Col. 1527D] and after our prohibitions; but consider it yourself in your mind, and determine and judge in your conscience whether you have acted well.

But since we neither can nor ought to pass with deaf ears over the cries of those brethren and the contempt shown to the Apostolic See, although even now our commands may seem to be poured forth in vain, by these apostolic letters we command your brotherhood and, by virtue of obedience, order you that—even if you should be absent from your Church—you shall without delay, at your own expense, demolish whatever has been done after the appeal made to us or after our prohibition in the work of the chapel which you resolved to erect for the destruction of the monastery of Canterbury; and that you shall revoke and render altogether void [Col. 1528A] whatever has been done and unlawfully innovated concerning the establishment of canons and other matters around the chapel.
